records.title: Samuel A. Green Scholarship Program
records.description: The Daniel B. and Florence E. Green Foundation has established a scholarship program to current residents or students who attend school within the Greater Philadelphia and Lehigh Valley areas and who plan to continue their education in a non-for-profit college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Samuel A. Green Scholarship Program must: Be a legal resident of the United States – including U.S. citizens, permanent residents, and others lawfully residing in the country Be a high school graduating senior (can be from public, private, parochial, charter schools, home-schooled students), technical school graduates and GED recipients, and be under twenty-five (25) years old as of January 11, 2027 Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited not-for-profit community or four-year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year Reside or attend school within the Greater Philadelphia and Lehigh Valley areas (specifically: Bucks County, Chester County, Delaware County, Lehigh County, Montgomery County, Northampton County, and Philadelphia County in Pennsylvania; Camden County, Gloucester County, Burlington County, and Salem County in New Jersey; New Castle County in Delaware) Employees, officers and directors of The Daniel B. and Florence E. Green Foundation, its subsidiaries, affiliates, donors, distributors, advertising and promotion agencies and their family members (defined as spouses, children, parents, siblings and in-laws) and those living in their households are not eligible. This exclusion also applies to anyone who may become an employee of The Daniel B. and Florence E. Green Foundation or such subsidiaries, affiliates, donors, distributors, and advertising and promotion agencies after submitting their application.

records.title: Chi-Rise Emergency Aid
records.description: Crown Family Philanthropies on behalf of Arie and Ida Crown Memorial has established a grant program for active Chi-Rise Scholarship recipients currently enrolled in school who are experiencing a financial difficulty that may negatively impact their enrollment in college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants for Chi-Rise Emergency Aid must: Be an active Chi-Rise Scholarship Recipient Be a current college undergraduate student enrolled full-time Have unexpected financial difficulties that may impact enrollment in school Be able to upload a course schedule* to verify full-time enrollment Be able to upload documentation of an eligible expense** *Course schedule must include the student’s first and last name, school name, current semester, courses, and credit hours for each course. ** Applicants must have incurred eligible expenses within thirty (30) days of application submission to be considered for reimbursement. Expenses are for one-time, emergency need situations and are not meant to address long-standing challenges. Students may only select one (1) eligible expense category on the application. Acceptable documentation for eligible expenses includes bills, invoices, and receipts. Documentation must include the student’s first and last name; vendor or payee name, physical address and/or URL, and phone number; itemized list of expense(s); and total expense. Eligible Expenses (for student only, not family members): Off-campus housing/rent/utilities (for utilities only – the lesser of three (3) months utility costs or the maximum award amount) Medical/dental (including school-required medical insurance if not already calculated in the student’s Chi-Rise Scholarship award amount for 2025 and 2026 high school graduates) Childcare Transportation/car repair (not gas, insurance, or regular maintenance – expense should be an unexpected repair or emergency situation) Food/groceries (not school-associated meal plans) Public transportation/travel (does not include public transportation passes required by the school if included in the calculation of the student’s Chi-Rise Scholarship for 2025 and 2026 high school graduates) Technology/computer/Wi-Fi Device grants are limited to a one-time award per student’s academic lifetime, specifically intended to fund the repair or replacement of broken or non-functional technology. Ineligible Expenses: Books Tuition and fees Required course materials On-campus housing Expenses calculated as part of the student’s Chi-Rise Scholarship (2025 and 2026 high school graduates)

records.title: Achieve Atlanta Emergency Grant
records.description: Achieve Atlanta has established a grant program for eligible or active Achieve Atlanta scholars currently enrolled in school who are experiencing a financial difficulty that may negatively impact their enrollment in college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Achieve Atlanta Emergency Grant must: Be a current Achieve Atlanta ‘active’* Scholar or be deemed eligible by Achieve Atlanta Applicants NOT on the original master list of eligible applicants will be escalated back to Achieve Atlanta to determine eligibility Be currently enrolled in school at the time of application Have an unexpected eligible financial expense that may impact enrollment or persistence in school Upload documents to verify identity and eligible expenses (e.g. bills, invoices, receipts) *An Achieve Atlanta ‘active’ Scholar is defined as a Scholar who is enrolled and receiving Achieve Atlanta scholarship funds for the current semester. Achieve Atlanta will provide SAI with the list of eligible ‘active’ Scholars. Eligible Expenses Achieve Atlanta will provide SAI a list of specific eligible expense categories and guidelines as needs and priorities change. These specific eligible expenses will fall into the following broad categories: Housing Utilities Medical/Dental Childcare Transportation Moving Internet/Wi-Fi Food ($300 maximum grant) Other as determined by Achieve Atlanta Ineligible expenses Tuition and fees Non-essential travel, including Study Abroad Technology Books Extra Spending Money Not Associated with an Emergency Expense

records.title: The Milliman Opportunity Scholarship – Non-U.S. Program
records.description: Milliman has established a scholarship program to assist high school/upper or higher secondary seniors or current undergraduate students living in and attending a university in Canada, Ireland, the United Kingdom, South Africa, or Australia.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to The Milliman Opportunity Scholarship – Non-U.S. Program must be: Belong to a qualified ethnic minority group*: In Canada, eligible candidates must have at least one birth parent who is a member of one of the following groups: African descent, Latino/Hispanic, Native North American, or Pacific Islander. In the UK and Ireland, eligible candidates must have at least one birth parent who is a member of one of the following groups: Black African, Black Caribbean, Irish Traveller or Romani. In South Africa, eligible candidates must have at least one birth parent who is a member of one of the following groups: Black or Coloured. In Australia, eligible candidates must have at least one birth parent who is a member of one of the following groups: Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander. Be living and attending a university in Canada, Ireland, the United Kingdom, South Africa or Australia. Be majoring or intending to major in one of the following fields of study: Actuarial Science Computer Science Data Analytics Data Science Economics Finance Mathematics Programming Statistics Be a high academically achieving student. Be a high school senior/higher or upper secondary student or a current postsecondary undergraduate. Students must be in their final year of upper or higher secondary school or be current technical or university level students. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited or bona fide college or university. In Canada, Ireland or the United Kingdom, the enrollment period is the Spring 2027 semester. In South Africa or Australia, the enrollment period is the first semester of 2027. *Minority Profile as defined by Milliman: Applicants should be students from qualifying ethnic groups who have historically been under-represented in the fields of actuarial science, data analytics, data science, computer science, economics, finance, mathematics, programming and statistics.

records.title: Nick and Karen Schmit Scholarship Program
records.description: The Nick and Karen Schmit Scholarship Program was established to assist high school seniors attending Harding Senior High School in St. Paul, MN who plan to continue their education in college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Nick and Karen Schmit Scholarship Program must: Be high school seniors attending Harding Senior High School in St. Paul, Minnesota. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited four-year college for the entire upcoming academic year.

records.title: Colin “Moon” Feltis Memorial Esports Scholarship
records.description: Kristy and Troy Feltis have established a scholarship program to assist current seniors on the Esports teams at World Scholars in Edinburg, Texas or Science Academy in Mercedes, Texas who plan to continue their education. Donations are accepted throughout the year. Please consider contributing to the Colin “Moon” Feltis Memorial Esports Scholarship. Donate Teen killed in Donna expressway crash remembered as talented gamer who spread kindness
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Colin “Moon” Feltis Memorial Esports Scholarship must: Be South Texas ISD high school seniors at World Scholars in Edinburg, Texas or Science Academy in Mercedes, Texas. Be members of the Esports team at one of the above high schools and be able to upload a letter or certificate from a school counselor to show participation Plan to enroll in full-time or part-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year Have a minimum grade point average of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent)

records.title: Jon G Carlstrom Family Scholarship
records.description: The Jon G. Carlstrom Family Trust has established a scholarship program for current high school seniors attending either Cleveland High School in Cleveland, MN or Bayfield High School in Bayfield, WI who plan to continue their education in college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Jon G Carlstrom Family Scholarship must: Be current high school seniors at either Cleveland High School (Cleveland, MN) or Bayfield High School (Bayfield, WI) Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year (2026-2027) Have a minimum grade point average of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent)

records.title: Vertex Foundation Scholarship for SCD & TDT Scholars
records.description: The Vertex Foundation Scholarship for SCD & TDT helps people with sickle cell disease (SCD) or transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia (TDT) and their immediate families (spouses, siblings, caregivers and children) pursue two-year, three-year, four-year or graduate degrees by offsetting some of the cost of attending college or graduate school.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Vertex Foundation Scholarship Program must: Be a United States or Canadian citizen or a foreign national lawfully admitted to the United States or Canada for permanent residence Be high school seniors/students in their final year of upper or higher secondary school, high school/upper or higher secondary school graduates, current technical or college/university undergraduate, and graduate level students in good academic standing Plan to enroll in part-time or full-time undergraduate or graduate study at an accredited two-, three- or four-year college or university, CEGEP institution (or equivalent) in the United States or Canada for the entire upcoming academic year Consent to disclose any information you provide with Scholarship America, Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated, the Vertex Foundation, and the academic institution And one of the following: Be diagnosed with sickle cell disease OR Be diagnosed with transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia OR Be an immediate* family member of an individual who has been diagnosed with sickle cell disease or transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia. *Immediate family members are defined as siblings, caregivers, children or spouses. Vertex Pharmaceuticals and Vertex Foundation employees, contractors, former employees, employee dependents and immediate family members are ineligible.

records.title: Charles L. Shor Foundation Epilepsy Scholarship
records.description: The Charles L. Shor Scholarship Fund has established a scholarship program for students currently being treated for active epilepsy seizures who plan to continue their education in college/vocational or trade school.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Charles L. Shor Foundation Epilepsy Scholarship must: Be a legal resident of the United States (U.S.) Have physician-documented, active epilepsy seizures within the previous 12 months as of the application deadline, not be a candidate for surgery, and be currently on medication to treat epilepsy. High school senior, high school graduate (including GED), or current college undergraduate Have not previously earned a bachelor’s degree, unless the applicant is seeking to enroll in a trade or vocational school program Plan to enroll in full-time or part-time* undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school in the U.S. for the entire upcoming academic year. *Part-time is defined as at least 6 credit hours per semester. Vocational/Trade School students are also encouraged to apply. Employees, their family members, officers, and directors of the Charles L. Shor Scholarship Fund, Epilepsy Wellness Advocates, or the Charles L. Shor Scholarship Fund are ineligible to apply.

records.title: Mattie Prescott “Be the Light” Memorial Scholarship
records.description: The Mattie Prescott “Be the Light” Memorial Scholarship was established to assist high school seniors at Grace Preparatory Academy or Matthew Road Academy in Texas who plan to continue their education in college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Mattie Prescott “Be the Light” Memorial Scholarship must: Be high school seniors at Grace Preparatory Academy or Matthew Road Academy in Texas Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year Have a minimum grade point average of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) Be recommended by their counselor, principal, or head of school at Grace Prep or Matthew Road

records.title: Brad Evans Scholarship Fund
records.description: Orange County Community Foundation has established a scholarship program for high school seniors in the Newport-Mesa Unified School District who have been accepted into the University of California, Berkeley.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Brad Evans Scholarship Fund must: Be high school seniors of an Orange County high school in the Newport-Mesa Unified School District Be a student who has been accepted to an accredited program at the University of California, Berkeley and plans to enroll as a full-time student for the upcoming Fall term Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent)

records.title: W.C. Stillwell Foundation Scholarship
records.description: The W.C. Stillwell Foundation Scholarship was established for current undergraduate students, college graduates, or current graduate students in a Doctor of Medicine program, who are seeking their Doctor of Medicine (MD) or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO) degree in medical school for the upcoming academic year.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the W.C. Stillwell Foundation Scholarship must: Have grown up* and graduated from a high school in one of the Southern Minnesota counties: Renville, Lincoln, Lyon, Redwood, Sibley, Brown, Nicollet, Le Sueur, Rice, Pipestone, Murray, Cottonwood, Watonwan, Blue Earth, Waseca, Steele, Rock, Nobles, Jackson, Martin, Faribault, or Freeborn *Definition of grown up – have lived the majority of their life in one of the listed counties Be a current college undergraduate, college graduate, or current graduate student in a Doctor of Medicine program Plan to be enrolled in full-time graduate study seeking their Doctor of Medicine (MD) or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine (DO) degree for the entire upcoming academic year at an accredited medical school

records.title: BURGER KING℠ Scholars
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants must meet the following criteria: BURGER KING ® General Track – Available to all high school seniors or past recipients who meet the criteria below. Applicant Requirements- Be living in the United States, Puerto Rico, Guam or Canada Have a cumulative high school grade point average of 2.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale, or the equivalent Plan to enroll full-time, without interruption, for the entire 2027-28 academic year at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school or CEGEP or equivalent in the U.S., Puerto Rico, Guam or Canada AND Be first-time applicants who are graduating 2027 high school seniors (U.S., Puerto Rico, and Guam), graduating from grade 12 (Canada) or graduating from homeschool education in the U.S., Puerto Rico, Guam, or Canada OR Be a past recipient of the Burger King Scholarship who is a current college undergraduate BURGER KING ® Employee-Based Track Note: The Employee-Based Track will have two components as follows. 1) Employees, spouses or domestic partners of employees, and dependent children of employees pursuing a traditional postsecondary education Applicant Requirements- Be living in the United States, Puerto Rico, Guam or Canada Be an employee* of Burger King Company LLC or a participating BURGER KING ® Franchisee OR Be a spouse (unless legally separated) or domestic partner** of an employee* of Burger King Company LLC or Franchisees OR Be a dependent child*** of an employee* of Burger King Company LLC or Franchisees AND Be graduating high school seniors (U.S., Puerto Rico and Guam) or have attained a GED, graduating from grade 12 (Canada), graduating from home school education in the U.S., Puerto Rico or Canada or current college undergraduates or graduate level students in the U.S., Puerto Rico, Guam or Canada Have a cumulative grade point average of 2.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale or the equivalent Plan to enroll part-time or full-time, without interruption for the 2027-28 academic year at an accredited two or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school or CEGEP or equivalent in the U.S., Puerto Rico, Guam or Canada 2) Employees and spouses or domestic partners of employees pursuing an enrichment program (Enrichment programs include, but are not limited to, language, computer and accounting courses.) Applicant Requirements- Be living in the United States, Puerto Rico, Guam or Canada Be an employee* of Burger King Company LLC or a participating BURGER KING ® Franchisee (Franchisees) OR Be a spouse (unless legally separated) or domestic partner** of an employee* of Burger King Company LLC or Franchisee (Designated Employer) AND Plan to enroll less than part-time or on an intermittent basis in GED, enrichment, certification or other course that enhances learning during the 2027-28 academic year (Note: Program or course must be taken at an accredited institution in the U.S., Puerto Rico, Guam or Canada.) * Employees must be active on Designated Employer’s payroll for at least 3 months as of the application deadline date and employed at the time awards are verified. ** Domestic partner is defined as (i) Employee’s sole Domestic Partner and intend to remain so indefinitely; (ii) Employee and Domestic Partner reside together in the same principal residence and intend to reside together indefinitely; (iii) Employee and Domestic Partner are both at least eighteen (18) years old and mentally competent to consent to a contract; (iv) Employee and Domestic Partner are not related by blood in a close enough manner that would bar marriage under applicable law in effect where they reside; and (v) Employee and Domestic Partner are not legally married to anyone else and are not involved in any other Domestic Partnership. *** Dependent children are defined as biological, step- or legally adopted children living in the employee’s household or primarily supported by the employee. Applicable to all tracks: Access to the application will remain open until the deadline. However, Scholarship America will only review the first 30,000 community applications received and will review all Employee applicants across all tracks. Any additional applications will not be reviewed or considered, even if submitted by the deadline.

records.title: Smart Futures for Small Business Scholarship
records.description: The Smart Futures for Small Business Scholarship program will offer $250-$1,000 to eligible small business employees who intend to enroll in a full-time or part-time artificial intelligence (AI) certification program in the United States by September 1, 2026, and complete it by December 31, 2026.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Smart Futures for Small Business Scholarship must: Be a legal resident of the United States (U.S.) and at least 18 years of age Be a small business* employee in the U.S. *Small business is defined as an independent company that is for-profit and has 500 or fewer employees. Franchises are not eligible for this program. Plan to enroll in a full-time or part-time AI certification program in the U.S. by September 1, 2026, and complete it by December 31, 2026 Plan to have between $250 and $1,000 in eligible educational costs for enrollment in an AI certification program offered by an accredited two- or four-year college, university, vocational-technical school, or AI educational vendor Employees, officers, and directors of Scholarship America, American Express, and their respective affiliates, as well as their immediate family members (spouses, parents, children, siblings, and their respective spouses, regardless of where they reside) and individuals living in the same household, whether or not related, are ineligible to apply. Examples of eligible AI certification programs include: AI for Business/Business Professionals/Business Leaders AI for Marketing & Sales AI in Business & Finance AI Starter Paths Advanced Prompt Engineering for Business Users Artificial Intelligence: Implications for Business Strategy Business Intelligence Data Analytics for Business Essential AI Skills Generative AI for Business Applications Introduction to Generative AI Real-World AI for Everyone

records.title: California Water Service Group Scholarship Program
records.description: The California Water Service Group has established a scholarship program to assist students residing within its service areas who plan to continue their education in college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic To be eligible for this scholarship program: Applicants must be a minimum of 16 years of age and a high school senior, high school graduate, have received GED certification, or be a current postsecondary undergraduate student. Applicant or applicant’s parents or guardians must live within a Cal Water Service Company, Hawaii Water Service Company, New Mexico Water Service Company, or Washington Water Service Company service area at the time of application. Applicants must plan to enroll in a full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Applicants must not have already received a bachelor’s degree from a four-year college or university. Applicants must not be the child of a current or former employee of the California Water Service Group or any of its subsidiaries, or a member of its Board of Directors. Non-traditional students who are returning to school or planning to pursue a post-secondary education for the first time are eligible and encouraged to apply. To verify that you or your parent or guardians live in one of the eligible service areas, click the appropriate link below: California Water Service (Cal Water) service areas Hawaii Water Service (Hawaii Water) service areas New Mexico Water Service (New Mexico Water) service areas Washington Water Service (Washington Water) service areas wysiwyg_basic

records.title: Edison Scholars Program
records.description: Edison Scholars was created to recognize the makers of tomorrow – students with big dreams to help power the future. The program awards college scholarships to help fuel your passion for making a difference by studying science, technology, engineering and math.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Edison Scholars program applicants must: Be a current high school senior with a cumulative grade point average of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale or the equivalent. Live in Southern California Edison’s (SCE) service area. Have an SCE Customer Number from the family’s SCE utility bill Plan to attend a full-time undergraduate course of study at an accredited four-year college or university in the U.S. for the 2027-2028 academic year. Plan to enroll in an eligible major in computer and information systems, engineering, engineering technology, management information systems, mathematics, natural resources and conservation, or physical sciences. Demonstrate a need for financial assistance. Dependents of Edison International and SCE employees or retirees are not eligible for the Edison Scholars program.

records.title: Howard Hughes Communities™ Scholarship Program
records.description: Howard Hughes Communities™, the real estate platform of Howard Hughes Holdings (NYSE: HHH), creates vibrant, award-winning communities where people can live their best lives. To support generations to come, the Howard Hughes Communities Scholarship Program will award three renewable $5,000 scholarships to high school seniors residing in or around one of their communities.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Howard Hughes Communities Scholarship Program must: Be high school seniors, high school graduates or current college undergraduates residing in one of the following five (5) regional areas: Maryland – Howard County Texas – Harris or Montgomery Counties Nevada – Clark County Arizona – Maricopa County Hawaii – Honolulu County Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) Be pursuing a major in one of the following fields: Real Estate/Construction, Sustainability, Accounting, Marketing/Digital, Finance/Economics, Technology, Engineering (Civil/Mechanical), Human Resources, Communication, English/Literature

records.title: Sasol Scholars Program: 2026 Community Scholarship
records.description: Sasol launched the Sasol Scholars Program with the 2026 Community Scholarship for students interested in pursuing higher education. This opportunity-embedded award provides up to $75,000 in scholarships to high school seniors graduating from Sasol partner schools in Louisiana. Students must plan to enroll in full-time associate or bachelor’s degree programs in Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, Business, Liberal Arts or related fields.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Sasol Community Scholarship Program must: Be a high school senior attending any school within the Calcasieu Parish School Board OR be a child of Sasol employees Have a cumulative GPA of 2.75 on a 4.0 scale or higher (or equivalent) Plan to enroll in full-time (minimum 12 credit hours or equivalent) undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Plan to pursue one of the following fields of study: Associate degree: Chemical Laboratory Technology Industrial Instrumentation Technology Industrial Electrical Technology Machine Tool Technology Process Technology Related fields Bachelor’s degree: Science Technology Engineering Mathematics Business Liberal Arts Related fields

records.title: The Paula Kovarick Segalman Family Scholarship for ALS
records.description: The EveryLife Foundation for Rare Diseases, alongside the Segalman family, has established a community scholarship program to provide financial assistance to students who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs and whose ability to cover the costs is severely compromised as a result of their family’s financial burden of ALS.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to The Paula Kovarick Segalman Family Scholarship for ALS must meet all of the following criteria: Be individuals who have had finances impacted due to having been diagnosed with ALS themselves, or a parent or guardian or immediate family member* (living or deceased) having been diagnosed with ALS. *Immediate family members refers to a person’s parent, spouse, sibling or parent’s spouse. Be high school seniors, high school graduates, GED holders, or current undergraduates. Plan to enroll in a full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-or-four year college, university or vocational school for the entire upcoming academic year. Be U.S. citizens. Current recipients of #RAREis Scholarship Fund are ineligible to receive an award for the #Paula Kovarick Segalman Family Scholarship for ALS.

records.title: Empowered Fathers in STEM Scholarship
records.description: Carr-Reza Family Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist fathers with dependent children who are seeking a Bachelor’s, Master’s or Graduate degree in a STEM field.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Empowered Fathers in STEM Scholarship must meet all of the following criteria: Live in the Dallas, Texas area Be a father with dependent children* *Dependent children are defined as biological, step- or legally adopted children living in the father’s household or primarily supported by the father Plan to enroll in an accredited institution during the entire upcoming academic year to seek a Bachelor’s, Master’s or Graduate degree in a STEM field Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent)

records.title: Cleaveland/Price Inc. Scholarship
records.description: Cleaveland/Price Inc. has established a scholarship program to assist high school seniors attending in the following Pennsylvania school districts: Penn Trafford, Norwin, Gateway, Franklin Regional, Greensburg Salem, Hempfield, or Jeannette who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Cleaveland/Price Inc. Scholarship must: Be current high school seniors attending one of the following school districts in Pennsylvania: Penn Trafford, Norwin, Gateway, Franklin Regional, Greensburg Salem, Hempfield, or Jeannette. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Be pursuing an Engineering degree or Machine Technology or Machinist certificate or degree.

records.title: CRCA Foundation Scholarship Program
records.description: CRCA Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist current high school seniors in Cook or other Chicagoland area counties who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the CRCA Foundation Scholarship Program must: Be a high school senior Be a legal United States (U.S.) citizen residing in Cook or other Chicagoland area counties* Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year Have an ACT composite score of 28 or greater, or SAT composite score of 1300 or greater *Eligible Chicagoland area counties are: Illinois: Boone, Bureau, Carrol, Cook, DeKalb, DuPage, Ford, Grundy, Iroquois, Jo-Davess, Kanakee, Kane, Kendal, Lake, LaSalle, Lee, Livingston, McHenry, Ogle, Putman, Stephenson, Will, Winnebago. Indiana: Jasper, La Porte, Lake, Newton, Porter, Pulaski, Starke. Wisconsin: Columbia, Dane, Green, Iowa, Lafayette, Richland, Rock, Sauk.

records.title: Albemarle Community Scholarship
records.description: Albemarle Corporation has established a scholarship program to assist high school seniors in Cleveland County, North Carolina who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Albemarle Community Scholarship must: Be current high school seniors attending school in Cleveland County, North Carolina Plan to study a STEM major (medical majors are NOT eligible) Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent – unweighted scale) Albemarle Corporation employees and their immediate family members (spouses or dependents) are ineligible.

records.title: Dorothy Bratsas Scholarship Fund
records.description: The Greater New Orleans Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist female students who attended high school in the Greater New Orleans region who plan to continue their education in college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Dorothy Bratsas Scholarship Fund must be: A female high school senior, high school graduate or current undergraduate, who attended high school in Orleans or Jefferson Parish. Planning to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent).

records.title: Patterson Scholarship Program
records.description: Patterson Companies has established a scholarship program to assist students who plan to pursue or continue their higher education in college or vocational school programs with a focus on dental or veterinary medicine related field.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic To foster students in the field of veterinary and dental careers, we encourage applicants from underrepresented populations to apply for the Patterson Scholarship. To be eligible: Be a high school senior, graduate, or current college undergraduate Plan to pursue a degree in a dental or veterinary medicine related field Plan to enroll in full-time or half-time* in an undergraduate, associate, or certificate** study at an accredited two-or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year/term. Students currently pursuing a graduate level degree are not eligible to apply. *Half-time enrollment includes at least one or more courses with a minimum of 6 credit hours (or equivalent). **Certification programs must be through an accredited institution and must run on a standard academic semester calendar. Certification programs must be a minimum of one semester in length.

records.title: APF Community Scholarship Program
records.description: The Alabama Power Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist high school seniors residing within Alabama Power Company service territory who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the APF Community Scholarship Program must: Be current high school seniors. Reside in a county* in Alabama within the Alabama Power Company (APC) service territory. *Residents of the following counties in Alabama are outside of the APC service territory and are NOT eligible: Colbert, DeKalb, Jackson, Lauderdale, Limestone, Madison, Morgan and Pike. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent). Children of employees of Alabama Power Company or Alabama Power Foundation are ineligible.

records.title: First Sentier Foundation Scholarship Program
records.description: First Sentier Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist current undergraduate sophomores who plan to continue college at a 4-year college in New York City for the upcoming academic year with an interest in the financial services industry and pursuing an eligible major*.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the First Sentier Foundation Scholarship Program must: Be current sophomore college undergraduates in good academic standing as of the application deadline date. Be enrolled in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited four-year college or university in New York City for the upcoming academic year (2026-2027). Demonstrate an interest in financial services and studying an eligible major*. Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent). *Eligible majors to include: Finance, Business Management, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, Statistics, Data Analytics, Computer Science, Information Technology, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence in Finance, Compliance, and Risk Management. First Sentier Investors employees and their immediate family members (spouses and dependents) are ineligible.

records.title: Parent Booster USA Scholarship Program
records.description: Parent Booster USA has established a scholarship program to assist high school seniors and high school graduates who are associated with a Parent Booster USA member organization and plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Parent Booster USA Scholarship Program must meet all of the following: Be associated with a Parent Booster USA member organization* *Must provide Parent Booster USA member organization ID number Be high school seniors or high school graduates (who have graduated within one year) who are not currently enrolled in higher education. Students who have taken PSEO courses during high school are eligible to apply Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) Children of Parent Booster USA directors and personnel are ineligible.

records.title: William S. and Margaret I. Marvin Warroad Four-Year College Scholarship Program
records.description: Established by the Marvin family, the William S. and Margaret I. Marvin Warroad Scholarships recognize graduating Warroad High School seniors who exemplify the civic-mindedness of William S. and Margaret I. Marvin.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic William S. and Margaret I. Marvin Warroad Four-Year College Scholarship Program must: Be a graduating Warroad High School senior (class of 2026). Be enrolled full-time at Warroad High School during Junior and Senior year. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited four-year college, or university for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 2.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent). Grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and great-great grandchildren of William S. and Margaret I. Marvin are ineligible.

records.title: The Donald and Delores Boyle Scholarship
records.description: The Donald and Delores Boyle Scholarship Fund has established a scholarship program to assist high school seniors or graduates in the state of Connecticut who plan to continue their education in college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to The Donald and Delores Boyle Scholarship must: High school seniors or graduates, who reside in the state of Connecticut and plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university for the entire upcoming academic year Plan to purse a degree in a STEM field (Sciences, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics) Medical-related fields are not eligible.

records.title: Rotary Club of Saint Paul Second Century Scholarship Program
records.description: The Saint Paul Rotary Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist students from high schools in Saint Paul, Minnesota who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Rotary Club of Saint Paul Second Century Scholarship Program must: Have participated in Camp RYLA (Rotary Youth Leadership Awards) Be a current high school senior or recent graduate of a Saint Paul high school in Saint Paul, Minnesota Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent)

records.title: Education Scholarship for Wisconsin Sickle Cell Patients
records.description: A scholarship program has been established to assist students in the state of Wisconsin, who have been diagnosed by a physician with Sickle Cell Disease and plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Education Scholarship for Wisconsin Sickle Cell Patients must: High school seniors or graduates, or current postsecondary undergraduates, who plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 2.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) Be a resident of Wisconsin Have been diagnosed by a physician with Sickle Cell Disease (as part of the application, applicants will be required to upload a Diagnosis Verification Form completed by their doctor)

records.title: William P. and Elizabeth McDow Lurton Scholarship Program
records.description: The H. William Lurton Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist high school seniors attending Jerseyville High School who plan to pursue postsecondary education in college and vocational programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the William P. and Elizabeth McDow Lurton Scholarship Program must be: High school seniors attending Jerseyville High School, Jerseyville, IL. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire academic year.

records.title: National Charity League – Pacific Coast Chapter Scholarship
records.description: National Charity League, Inc., Pacific Coast Chapter has established a scholarship program to assist students who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the National Charity League – Pacific Coast Chapter Scholarship must: Be female Be a high school senior attending one of the following Huntington Beach Union High School District high schools: Edison High School Fountain Valley High School Huntington Beach High School Marina High School Ocean View High School Westminster High School Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited four-year college or university or a vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) Current or former Members of any Chapter of the National Charity League are ineligible.

records.title: Fredericksburg Scholarship Program
records.description: The Fredericksburg Scholarship Program was created to assist current high school seniors at Fredericksburg ISD who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school in Texas.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Fredericksburg Scholarship Program must: Be high school seniors at Fredericksburg ISD Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school in Texas for the entire upcoming academic year Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent)

records.title: West Texas Strong Memorial Scholarship Program
records.description: The Kent Companies have established a scholarship program to assist residents of Midland or Odessa, Texas, who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the West Texas Strong Memorial Scholarship Program must meet all of the following criteria: Be a current resident or currently be residing in Midland, TX or Odessa, TX. Plan to enroll in fulltime undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year.

records.title: Los Angeles County Committee of Bar Examiners Accredited Law Schools Scholarship
records.description: The University of West Los Angeles School of Law, Purdue Global Law School, and Santa Barbara and Ventura Colleges of Law have established the Los Angeles County Committee of Bar Examiners Accredited Law Schools Scholarship to assist students pursuing graduate study at the University of West Los Angeles School of Law, Purdue Global Law School (formerly Concord Law School: Purdue University Global), or Santa Barbara and Ventura Colleges of Law.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Los Angeles County Committee of Bar Examiners Accredited Law Schools Scholarship must be: In their final year of undergraduate study or currently enrolled in graduate study. records.title: Ernest C. Styberg Jr. Memorial Scholarship Program
records.description: The Ernest C. Styberg Jr. Memorial Scholarship Program was established by the E.C. Styberg Foundation, Inc. to assist graduating high school seniors in Kenosha (WI) or Racine (WI) counties who plan to attend full-time undergraduate study for the entire upcoming academic year.

records.eligibility: Award information: wysiwyg_basic If selected as a recipient, the student will receive notification of the amount of the award. Awards for Dunn and Pepin County students may be renewed for up to three additional years or until a bachelor’s degree is earned, whichever occurs first. Renewal is contingent upon satisfactory academic performance in full-time study in the specified area. Awards for family members are renewable for up to three years or until a bachelor’s degree is earned, whichever occurs first. Renewal is contingent upon satisfactory academic performance in full-time study. Renewal of scholarships for graduate study will be considered on a case-by-case basis. All renewals are contingent on continuation of the program by the sponsor. Note: Non Family Members’ declared major must remain in an agriculture-related, agribusiness or biological sciences (biology in regard to plants and animals) or scholarship award will be forfeited. Each year upon renewal this will be verified. Notification Applicants will be notified in May. Not all applicants to the program will be selected as recipients. Selection of recipients is made by Scholarship America. Neither James R. Truax nor any member of the Truax/Johnson family plays a part in the selection. All applicants agree to accept the decision as final. Notifications are sent via email. When setting up your account, avoid using a school or work email. Instead, use an active, personal email address that you will continue to have access to. Please make sure to add studentsupport@scholarshipamerica.org as well as the program email address as safe senders in your email contact list. Payment of Scholarships Scholarship America processes scholarship payments on behalf of the sponsor. Payments are made in one installment in early August. Scholarship recipients are selected on the basis of: Academic performance Demonstrated leadership, participation in school and community activities, awards and honors Work experience and/or home responsibilities Statement of career and educational aspirations and goals Unusual personal or family circumstances A brief statement answering the questions: How do you plan to pay for college? In what ways have you earned money for college expenses? An online recommendation (teacher, school counselor, work supervisor) Financial Information Selection of recipients is made by Scholarship America. Neither James R. Truax nor any member of the Truax/Johnson family plays a part in the selection. All applicants agree to accept the decision as final.
