records.title: Olympus Energy Scholarship Program
records.description: Olympus Energy has established a scholarship program to assist high school seniors in the greater Pittsburgh area.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Olympus Energy Scholarship Program must: Self-identify as Black or African American, American Indian or Alaska Native, Hispanic or Latino, Asian, Native Hawaiian or other Pacific Islander. Be residents of the following counties in the greater Pittsburgh area: Allegheny Armstrong Beaver Butler Fayette Greene Indiana Washington Westmoreland High school seniors who plan to enroll in part-time or full-time undergraduate study in a STEM-related program of study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent). Have never been convicted of a misdemeanor or felony crime. Current employees of Olympus Energy and their children are ineligible.

records.title: Hispanic Alliance GA Scholarship Program
records.description: Hispanic Alliance GA has established a scholarship program to assist students who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Hispanic Alliance GA Scholarship Program must: Be high school seniors that reside in Georgia Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year* Have a minimum grade point average of 2.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) *Certification programs must be through an accredited institution and must run on a standard academic semester calendar. Certification programs must be a minimum of one semester/term in length and recipients must be enrolled at the time awards are disbursed in August.

records.title: US Foods Scholars Program
records.description: US Foods, Inc. has established a scholarship program to assist students pursuing a degree in the Culinary Arts, Hospitality, or related disciplines.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the US Foods Scholars Program must: Be at least 18 years of age at the time awards are disbursed in August Be a legal U.S. resident or person authorized to work in the fifty (50) United States and the District of Columbia Plan to enroll or already enrolled in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year Be pursuing a Culinary Arts degree or a related discipline, including, but not limited to, Culinary Science, Baking and Pastry Arts, Nutrition and Food Business Management, or Hospitality Management Agree to participate in at least one professional development opportunity provided by US Foods US Foods employees, subsidiaries, parents, affiliates, representatives, consultants, contractors, legal counsel, advertising, public relations, promotional, fulfillment, and marketing agencies, and members of their immediate families (spouses, parents, siblings, and children, regardless of where they live) and those living in the same household are not eligible.

records.title: Student Volunteer Award
records.description: The Student Volunteer Award is a collection of named scholarship awards established to assist student volunteers who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Student Volunteer Award must: Be graduating high school seniors Be a part of a Dollars for Scholars supported service area and have applied for a Dollars for Scholars scholarship. Have community service/volunteer experience within four years as of the application deadline Have a cumulative GPA of 2.5 or higher Plan to attend an accredited two-year, four-year college or university, or a vocational-technical college in a full time course of study for the entire upcoming academic year

records.title: NetApp Scholarship
records.description: NetApp has established a scholarship program to assist current undergraduates enrolled at North Carolina A&T State University who plan to continue their education in an eligible major or course of study.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the NetApp Scholarship must: Be a current undergraduate sophomore or junior (2026-2027 academic year) Be enrolled in full-time undergraduate study at North Carolina Agricultural and Technical State University and study an eligible major listed below: Artificial Intelligence Business Analytics Business Information Technology Computer Science Electrical Engineering Information Technology Management Business Administration Management (Information Systems) Supply Chain Management Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent)

records.title: The cg42 Foundation Scholarship Program
records.description: cg42 is a New York-based management consulting firm. They take a human-centered approach to helping clients solve strategic business challenges. In that spirit, the cg42 Foundation aims to provide post-secondary education opportunities to students who demonstrate strong critical thinking skills, intellectual curiosity and an interest in human behavior.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to The cg42 Foundation Scholarship Program must: Be high school seniors (including homeschool students) in the U.S. Be U.S. citizens, nationals, permanent residents, refugees, asylees or humanitarian parolees Plan to pursue a major or minor in one of the following: Humanities, Liberal Arts, and Social Sciences Have a minimum grade point average of 3.5 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at one of the accredited four-year colleges or universities listed below for the entire upcoming academic year: columned_text Auburn University Boston College Drexel University Fairfield University George Mason University Hampton University Randolph-Macon College Stanford University Tulane University University of Dayton University of Georgia University of Notre Dame University of Southern California University of Texas at Austin Virginia Commonwealth University Williams College Yale University wysiwyg_basic Children of employees of The cg42 Foundation and cg42, LLC are ineligible.

records.title: Actuary of Tomorrow – Stuart A. Robertson Memorial Scholarship
records.description: Milliman has established a scholarship program to assist current undergraduates at a sophomore level or above who have successfully completed at least two actuarial exams and plan to continue their education college or university.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Actuary of Tomorrow – Stuart A. Robertson Memorial Scholarship must: Be a current college undergraduate with a minimum sophomore standing Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited four-year college or university in the United States (U.S.) for the upcoming academic year*. Must have successfully completed at least two actuarial exams Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) *Students graduating mid-year (after Fall term 2026) may be considered for a half-award

records.title: The William Gawor Perpetual Scholarship Program
records.description: The William Gawor Perpetual Scholarship Fund has established a scholarship program to assist high school seniors from Bayonne High School or Rahway High School in New Jersey who plan to major in a STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Math) field at a four-year university.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to The William Gawor Perpetual Scholarship Program must be: High school seniors from Bayonne High School or Rahway High School in New Jersey. Planning to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited four-year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year. Planning to major in a STEM* field (Science, Technology, Engineering and Math) of study in college. *This includes STEM programs or those which include elements of STEM. For example, Criminal Justice study requires knowledge of science and an understanding of technology used in the field. Applicants with questions regarding the eligibility of their field of study should refer the question to Scholarship America through their guidance counselor. Have a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.00 on a 4.00 scale (or the equivalent).

records.title: #RAREis Scholarship Fund
records.description: The EveryLife Foundation for Rare Diseases has established the #RAREis Scholarship Fund to help adults with rare diseases in a variety of educational pursuits, regardless of treatment status.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the #RAREis Scholarship Fund must be: U.S. residents who have been diagnosed* by a physician as having any form of rare disease regardless of treatment status. Applicants will be asked to provide a Diagnosis Verification Form provided by a physician verifying diagnosis. Currently enrolled or planning to enroll full-time or part-time** in undergraduate or graduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical/trade school for the Fall 2026 semester. 17 years old or older (no upper age limit, veterans and non-traditional students are encouraged.) *Undiagnosed applicants may apply with completed Diagnosis Verification Form by a physician. **There is no minimum amount of credit hours to be part-time (example, one class is considered part time).

records.title: SkyWater Foundation Scholarship Program
records.description: SkyWater Foundation Fund, Inc. has established a scholarship program to assist students who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the SkyWater Foundation Scholarship Program must: Be high school graduates and/or current college undergraduates, who plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school* for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) *Certification programs must be through an accredited institution and must run on a standard academic semester calendar. Certification programs must be a minimum of one semester/term in length and applicants must be enrolled at the time awards are disbursed in August 2026. Oxbow Industries and SkyWater Technology employees and their children are eligible to apply, though they will not be given preference.

records.title: Holt College Scholarship
records.description: The Holt College Scholarship is a program designed to assist residents of Louisiana who plan to continue their education in college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants of the college scholarship program must be: Residents of Louisiana by the application deadline High school seniors or current college undergraduates Planning to enroll in full-time study at an eligible* postsecondary institution the entire upcoming academic year Have a minimum grade point average of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) *Eligible postsecondary institutions includes: accredited two-year or four-year college or university, or vocational-technical college.

records.title: LPA Diversity in Design Scholarship Program
records.description: LPA, Inc. has established a scholarship program to champion the design professions among students from underrepresented demographics.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the LPA Diversity in Design Scholarship Program must: Be high school seniors or graduates or current college undergraduates Live in California or Texas Have been accepted in a full-time undergraduate study at an accredited NAAB, LAAB, ABET, CIDA, NASAD, four- or five-year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year Pursuing a bachelor’s degree in one of the following majors associated with the building and design industry: Architecture, Landscape Architecture, Interior Architecture/Design, Architectural Engineering, Structural Engineering, Building Science, Civil Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related degree Be a student who has overcome significant challenges in their academic pursuit and/or belong to a group historically underrecognized or marginalized within the building and design industry Be legally authorized to work in the United States

records.title: USPA Intercollegiate Scholarship Program
records.description: U.S. Polo Association has established a scholarship program to assist USPA members who plan to continue their education in college programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the USPA Intercollegiate Scholarship Program must meet all the following criteria: Be a current USPA member in good standing. Be a high school senior or graduate, or current postsecondary undergraduate. Be or have been an active team member of an interscholastic polo program at the time of application, competing in at least two of four years of their high school career, with priority going to players who competed in their senior year, as proven by appearing on their team’s USPA official IS Team Roster and on USPA I/I Official score sheets for that team, in an official Qualified game, in which the applicant plays, for each year. Current intercollegiate players must be an active team member with an existing intercollegiate polo program, as proven by appearing on their team’s USPA official IC team roster and appear on at least one USPA I/I Official score sheet for that team, in the current academic year. *Current intercollegiate players must also meet the interscholastic polo requirement. Plan to enroll in full time undergraduate study at an accredited four year college or university with an existing intercollegiate polo program for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) and be in good standing with your college or university. Each applicant’s membership will be pre-verified by the Sponsor before selection process.

records.title: Charles Esplin Scholarship
records.description: PNC Bank, N.A., as trustee of the Charles Esplin Trust has established a scholarship program for Rock Island High School (District #41) who plan to continue their education in college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Charles Esplin Scholarship must: Be high school seniors at Rock Island High School – District #41 Rank in the upper 25% of the graduating class at the end of the seventh semester Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year* *No gaps allowed – must be attending in Fall 2026 PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply

records.title: NSA Scholarship Program
records.description: The National Supermarket Association Scholarship Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist those students within the local communities in which our member stores are located. Through education we are empowering our communities for a brighter future.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the NSA Scholarship Program must: Be high school seniors or graduates, current postsecondary undergraduates, or graduate students who plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate or graduate study or at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or graduate school for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 2.8 on a 4.0 scale or its equivalent Be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident of an individual granted deferred action status under the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals Program (DACA) Live in a NSA Service Area in New York, New Jersey or Connecticut Employees of NSA stores are eligible to apply. National Supermarket Association (NSA) store owners and immediate family members* of NSA storeowners are ineligible. *Immediate family members are defined as biological, step- or legally adopted children or Spouses of the storeowners.

records.title: RARE Scholars Program
records.description: BioMarin Pharmaceutical Inc. has established the RARE Scholars Program to assist high school seniors or graduates, current college undergraduates, or graduate level students who have been diagnosed by a physician, regardless of treatment status, with one of the following – achondroplasia, Batten disease, any form of mucopolysaccharidoses (MPS), or phenylketonuria (PKU) – or students who are a legal guardian of a child/individual diagnosed with one of the aforementioned conditions.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the RARE Scholars Program must: Be diagnosed by a physician, regardless of treatment status, with one of the following – achondroplasia, Batten disease, any form of mucopolysaccharidoses (MPS), or phenylketonuria (PKU) – or be a legal guardian of a child/individual diagnosed with one of the aforementioned conditions. Applicants will be asked to provide a Diagnosis Verification Form, for themselves or their child, provided by a physician verifying diagnosis. Be high school seniors or graduates, current college undergraduates, or graduate level students. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate or graduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent). Applicants are not required to be using a BioMarin product. Treatment status with any manufacturer products should not be disclosed and will not be considered in evaluating applications. BioMarin Pharmaceutical Inc. employees and their children are ineligible for the program.

records.title: Sardi’s Scholarship in Memorial of Philip G Sardelis
records.description: Sardi’s Holdings has established a scholarship program in Memorial of Philip G Sardelis to assist high school seniors, graduates and undergraduates.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Sardi’s Scholarship in Memorial of Philip G. Sardelis must: Reside within 10 miles of any Sardi’s Pollo a La Brasa restaurant.* Be high school seniors, high school graduates, or current college/university students. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college or university for the upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 2.5 or above on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent). Employees of Sardi’s and their children are ineligible. *Sardi’s Pollo a La Brasa locations: Alexandria, VA; Beltsville, MD; Bowie, MD; Capitol Heights, MD; Clinton, MD; Frederick, MD; Gaithersburg, MD; Glen Burnie, MD; Hagerstown, MD; Laurel, MD; New Carrollton, MD; Olney, MD; Oxon Hill, MD; Rockville, MD; Takoma Park/Langley Park, MD; Temple Hills, MD; Philadelphia, PA.

records.title: Firehouse Subs Public Safety Foundation Scholarship Program
records.description: Firehouse Subs Public Safety Foundation (Public Charity) has established a scholarship program to assist students who plan to enroll in a part-time or full-time firefighter, law enforcement, or emergency medical (paramedic or EMT) program at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school in the U.S. for the entire upcoming academic year.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Community applicants interested in applying for the Firehouse Subs Public Safety Foundation Scholarship must: Be a high school senior or graduate, or a current college undergraduate, and Plan to enroll in a part-time or full-time firefighter, law enforcement, or emergency medical (paramedic or EMT) program at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school in the U.S. for the entire upcoming academic year and Plan to pursue a career as a first responder (firefighter, police officer, paramedic or EMT). Firehouse Subs employee applicants interested in applying for the Firehouse Subs Public Safety Foundation Scholarship must: Be a Firehouse Subs employee who has a minimum of six months employment with the company as of the application deadline, and Be a high school senior or graduate, or current college undergraduate, and Plan to enroll in a part-time or full-time firefighter, law enforcement, or emergency medical (paramedic or EMT) program at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school in the U.S. for the entire upcoming academic year and Plan to pursue a career as a first responder (firefighter, police officer, paramedic or EMT).

records.title: The Janet Madori Scholarship Program
records.description: Kingdom Charitable Trust has established a scholarship program to assist students living in Florida who plan to continue their education in college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Janet Madori Scholarship Program must: Live in the state of Florida Be high school seniors Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited four-year college/university for the entire upcoming academic year Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale or its equivalent

records.title: The NextEra Energy Scholarship Awards
records.description: The NextEra Energy Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist eligible Florida high school seniors and undergraduates who plan to continue their education.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants for the Students in SECME Program must: Be a Florida high school senior residing in Brevard County, Broward County, Escambia County, Flagler County, Hendry County, Manatee County, Miami Dade County, Palm Beach County, Seminole County, or Volusia County Have at least one year involvement in SECME program in high school by the end of senior year Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year Have a minimum unweighted grade point average of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) Demonstrate as economically disadvantaged Be a Florida resident and the household must be served by Florida Power & Light Company (electrical service provider) Children of NextEra Energy and Florida Power & Light Company employees are ineligible. Applicants for the FPL Trade and Technical Program must: Be a Florida resident enrolled full-time at an accredited Florida trade school, community college, or technical center (individuals that can show proof of enrollment are eligible too) Be in pursuit of certificates/degrees in: Trade: Electrical Technology, Power Plant Operations, Solar Energy Systems, HVAC, Substations, Wind Turbines, Industrial Maintenance, Welding, or Instrumentation & Controls Technical: Electrical, Mechanical, Environmental, and Industrial Energy Systems, Computer/Network Systems Technology, Cybersecurity, Industrial Automation Technology, Data Analytics/SCADA Systems, or Environmental Engineering Have a minimum unweighted grade point average of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) Have an acceptance letter or articulation agreement with Florida college/university Submit a career goal essay of interest in an energy sector Demonstrate as economically disadvantaged Be a Florida resident and the household must be served by Florida Power & Light Company (electrical service provider) Have at least one year involvement in energy-related organizations or projects Children of NextEra Energy and Florida Power & Light Company employees are ineligible. Applicants for the FPL Workforce Ready Undergraduate Program must: Be a Florida resident enrolled in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited Florida college/university Be pursuing a degree in the energy industry Have a minimum unweighted grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) Have completed minimum twenty-four (24) credit hours Have an acceptance letter or articulation agreement with Florida college/university Submit a career goal essay of interest in an energy sector Demonstrate as economically disadvantaged Be a Florida resident and the household must be served by Florida Power & Light Company (electrical service provider) Have at least one year involvement in energy-related organizations or projects Children of NextEra Energy and Florida Power & Light Company employees are ineligible. Applicants for the FPL Workforce Ready Associates Program must: Be a Florida resident enrolled full-time in an associate’s degree program at an accredited Florida community college, state college, or technical college Be pursuing a degree in the energy industry Have a minimum unweighted grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) Have completed a minimum of nine (9) credit hours Have an acceptance letter or articulation agreement with Florida college/university Submit a career goal essay of interest in an energy sector Have demonstrated interest in energy sector careers Demonstrate as economically disadvantaged Be a Florida resident and the household must be served by Florida Power & Light Company (electrical service provider) Have at least one year involvement in energy-related organizations or projects Children of NextEra Energy and Florida Power & Light Company employees are ineligible.
records.award_amount: $5,000 annually and renewable up to four years for a maximum award of $20,000

records.title: Joe Lieberman Connecticut Scholarship Program
records.description: The Joe Lieberman Connecticut Scholarship Fund assists outstanding high school seniors from Connecticut who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Joe Lieberman Connecticut Scholarship Program must: Be United States citizens or permanent legal residents. Be high school seniors who reside in Connecticut and attend public or private high schools or home school in Connecticut. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 3.8 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent). Demonstrate outstanding leadership potential and a record of community service.

records.title: William Pablo Feraldo Memorial Foundation Scholarship Program
records.description: U.S. Bank, as Trustee of the William Pablo Feraldo Memorial Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist male students from high schools in the St. Louis Metropolitan area who plan to continue their education at an accredited four-year college or university.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to The William Pablo Feraldo Memorial Foundation Scholarship must: Be male high school seniors attending a high school in the St. Louis Metropolitan area. This includes high schools in Franklin County, Jefferson County, St. Charles County, St. Louis County, and the City of St. Louis in Missouri. In Illinois, this includes high schools in Madison County, Monroe County, and St. Clair County. Be planning to enroll or already enrolled in a full-time course of undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year. (Excluding Washington University in St. Louis and St. Louis University where separate William Pablo Feraldo Memorial Foundation Scholarship Programs are administered.) Demonstrate financial need as calculated by Scholarship America. Be recommended by a school official.

records.title: The Edwin E. and Janet L. Bryant Foundation, Inc. Scholarship Program
records.description: The Edwin E. and Janet L. Bryant Foundation, Inc. has established a scholarship program to assist former students of select Wisconsin communities’ high schools listed below. Renewable scholarships are offered each year for full-time or part-time study at an accredited institution of the student’s choice.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the The Edwin E. and Janet L. Bryant Foundation, Inc. Scholarship Program must: Be current postsecondary undergraduates or high school graduates. Applicants must have at least a high school diploma or GED certificate. Current high school students are not eligible to apply. Have graduated from one of the following high schools in Wisconsin or attended one of these high schools before obtaining a GED: Arcadia High School, Arcadia Black River Falls High, Black River Falls Bloomer High School, Bloomer Mineral Point High, Mineral Point Montello Junior/Senior High School, Montello Neillsville High School, Neillsville Riverdale Schools, Muscoda Stoughton High School, Stoughton Viroqua High School, Viroqua Wautoma High School, Wautoma Planning to enroll or currently enrolled in part-time or full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire academic year. Current high school seniors are not eligible to apply.

records.title: James and Thelma Connors Scholarship
records.description: The James & Thelma Connors Foundation established a scholarship program to assist students who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the James and Thelma Connors Scholarship must: Be a resident of the City of Medford, Massachusetts, attending or graduated from a public, private, charter, or secondary program in the city of Medford and surrounding area. Be a high school senior or graduate, age 21 and under, who will be entering their first year of undergraduate study in the Fall of 2026. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Be willing to attend an awards event in Medford, Massachusetts, upon invitation. Children and grandchildren of current James & Thelma Connors Foundation Directors are ineligible to apply.

records.title: The PIMCO Foundation Future Leaders Scholarship Program
records.description: A scholarship program for undergraduate students pursuing a degree and/or future career in the financial services industry.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to The PIMCO Foundation Future Leaders Undergraduate Scholarship must: Be a current college undergraduate sophomore (graduating with a bachelor’s degree between December 2027 – June 2028) in good academic standing at an accredited United States (U.S) institution as of the application deadline Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited four-year college or university in the U.S. for the entire upcoming academic year (Proof of registration will be required.) Demonstrate an interest in financial services by: Pursuing a relevant degree, including but not limited to business management, finance, computer science, engineering, economics AND/OR Pursuing a career in financial services or an adjacent industry (e.g.: financial technology) PIMCO employees and their immediate family members (spouses, children, and grandchildren) are ineligible.

records.title: The PIMCO Foundation Future Leaders Scholarship Program
records.description: A Scholarship program for graduate students pursuing a degree and/or future career in the financial services industry.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to The PIMCO Foundation Future Leaders Graduate Scholarship must: Plan to apply, be awaiting acceptance, or be accepted to a master’s degree program at an accredited United States (U.S.) institution for a Fall 2026 start (graduating with a master’s degree between December 2027 – June 2028) OR Be a doctoral student in good academic standing at an accredited U.S. institution with an expected graduation date between December 2027 – June 2028 Plan to enroll in full-time graduate study at an accredited four-year college or university in the U.S. for the entire upcoming academic year (Proof of acceptance and registration will be required.) Demonstrate an interest in financial services by: Pursuing a relevant degree, including but not limited to business management, finance, computer science, engineering, economics AND/OR Pursuing a career in financial services or an adjacent industry (e.g.: financial technology) PIMCO employees and their immediate family members (spouses, children, and grandchildren) are ineligible.

records.title: The Guild Giving National Scholarship
records.description: The Guild Giving National Scholarship was established for current undergraduate students, college graduates, or current graduate students pursuing a degree full-time in a collegiate program at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Eligibility Applicants to The Guild Giving National Scholarship must meet all of the following criteria: Be a United States citizen or national. Have a minimum grade point average of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale if applying as a four-year college student Be a high school senior or graduate, postsecondary undergraduate, or graduate student enrolled full-time in a collegiate program at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Applicants residing in New York are not eligible to apply.

records.title: Mason-Lite Architectural Scholarship Program
records.description: Masonry Fireplace Industries, Inc. has established a scholarship program to assist students who plan to pursue a degree in Architecture or Architectural Studies at an eligible college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Mason-Lite Architectural Scholarship Program must: High school seniors or graduates, or current postsecondary undergraduates Plan to pursue or are currently pursuing a degree in Architecture or Architectural Studies Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at one of the following universities: Cal Poly Pomona Rice University University of Colorado-Boulder University of North Carolina-Charlotte Carnegie Mellon University Have a minimum grade point average of 2.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent)

records.title: Athene Game Changer Scholarship Program
records.description: The Athene Charitable Foundation has established a scholarship program for students in Iowa that plan to continue their education at a two- or four-year college in Iowa.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Athene Game Changer Scholarship Program must meet all the following criteria: Be a U.S. citizen and Iowa resident. Be a high school senior or graduate or current college undergraduate. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university located in the state of Iowa for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale or its equivalent. Children of Athene employees are not eligible to apply.

records.title: The Adam Scripps Fredericksburg Excellence Award
records.description: The Adam R. Scripps Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist seniors in Fredericksburg Independent School District who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to The Adam Scripps Fredericksburg Excellence Award must: Reside in the State of Texas as of the application deadline date. Be high school seniors at Fredericksburg High School or Gillespie County High School in Fredericksburg Independent School District, Texas. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. (Preference will be given to students planning to attend schools in the state of Texas.)

records.title: TDECU Cares Foundation Student Member Scholarship Program
records.description: TDECU Cares Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist its Student Members to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the TDECU Cares Foundation Student Member Scholarship Program must: Be a TDECU or Space City Credit Union Student Member * in good standing as of the application deadline date. Be a current high school senior who plans to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. *The student’s account cannot be a TXUTMA (i.e. custodial account).

records.title: Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories Scholarship Program
records.description: The Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories scholarship program is open to current undergraduates attending eligible colleges and universities in the upcoming academic year and pursuing select science and engineering degrees.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories Scholarship Program must: Be current college undergraduates planning to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an eligible college for the entire upcoming academic year Eligible Colleges: Washington State University University of Idaho Montana Technological University Purdue University Michigan Technological University Boise State University Richmond Community College Drexel University University of North Carolina at Charlotte Georgia Institute of Technology Gonzaga University Mississippi State University Idaho State University (Only Robotics and Communications Systems Engineering Technology, 3-year program) Lewis Clark State College (Only Electrical Engineering Technology majors, 2-year program) Whitworth University (Only Engineering majors) Colorado School of Mines Penn State University Texas A&M University Be majoring in one of the following fields: Computer Engineering Computer Science Electrical Engineering Engineering (Whitworth University attendees only) Electrical Engineering Technology (Lewis Clark State College attendees only) Robotics and Communications Systems Engineering Technology (Idaho State University attendees only) Electric Utility Substation and Relay Technology (Richmond Community College attendees only)

records.title: Karl J. Schwartz Rotary Award Fund Scholarship Program

records.title: Penguin Random House Creative Writing Awards
records.description: Penguin Random House has established a scholarship program for high school seniors with outstanding creative writing skills who plan to continue their education in college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Penguin Random House Creative Writing Awards Program in Partnership with We Need Diverse Books must: Be current high school seniors at a public high school in the United States graduating Spring of 2027 Be 21 years of age and under Plan to enroll in an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or approved vocational-technical school Fall 2027 Submit one original* literary composition in English in one of the following genres of poetry, spoken word, fiction, personal essay/memoir, graphic novel, or book bans prompt. All submissions must be typed, double-spaced with a minimum 12 point font size and no longer than 10 pages. All submissions with multiple pages must be numbered with a page number and total number of pages (Ex. 1/3, 2/3, 3/3). A four-page minimum is recommended for the fiction genre. Spoken word entries must upload a typed entry along with an emailed audio format file. Only one entry per student may be submitted and considered. Graphic novel (a novel, usually in comics form, where the narrative is related through a combination of text and art, i.e. manga). Freedom of Expression entries must write about the provided topic. Book bans are on the rise in America, driven by new laws and regulations limiting the kinds of books young people can access—and books by and/or about LGBTQIA+ and BIPOC communities are disproportionately targeted. Penguin Random House and We Need Diverse Books believe books change lives, and that everyone deserves to see themselves in a book. Freedom of Expression Prompt: In the face of these book bans and attacks on free expression, we are celebrating the power of books and stories. Tell us about one banned book that changed your life and why. Only the first 1,000 applications will be accepted. Family members, employees of Bertelsmann, Penguin Random House, its subsidiaries, divisions or affiliates are ineligible. *Original compositions cannot be from class assignments, college essays, previous contests, or previous submissions. They must be unpublished works with no previous awards.

records.title: Ellevation Education Scholarship Program
records.description: Ellevation is the nation’s leading K-12 software solution for English Learners — built on the belief that every EL deserves the chance to achieve their highest aspirations. This scholarship program puts that belief into action, supporting students pursuing college or vocational school.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants of the Ellevation Education Scholarship Program must: Be high school seniors who have been enrolled as an English Language Learner (ELL) at some point during their K-12 education. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Children of employees of Ellevation Education and Curriculum Associates, LLC are ineligible to apply.

records.title: Margaret E. Oser Scholarship Fund
records.description: The Orange County Community Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist females currently enrolled at a Southern California – Orange County community college who plan to transfer to a four-year college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Margaret E. Oser Scholarship Fund must meet all of the following criteria: Identify as female. Be currently enrolled at one of the following Orange County community colleges (or had attended one of these schools and were previously awarded the Margaret E. Oser scholarship): Cypress College Fullerton College Santiago Canyon College Santa Ana College Saddleback College Golden West College Coastline Community College Orange Coast College Irvine Valley College Be planning to transfer to a four-year college or university (or have already transferred and were selected as a previous recipient) and will be enrolled full-time for the entire upcoming academic year. Must have completed at least two full-time enrollment semesters with 24 transferable credits to a four-year college or university. Have a minimum 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale. Declared a Major.

records.title: Miriam Bechtel Scholarship Foundation Fund
records.description: PNC Bank, N.A. Miriam Bechtel Scholarship Foundation Fund has established a scholarship program to assist students from designated Pennsylvania school districts who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs leading to a profession in nursing, medical, dental or osteopathy.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Miriam Bechtel Scholarship Foundation Fund must: Be current postsecondary undergraduates, high school seniors or graduates from the following school districts in Pennsylvania: Conewago Valley Area School District Gettysburg Area School District Hanover Public School District Littlestown Area School District Manchester Valley High School, Maryland South Western Public School District Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school in the United States for the entire upcoming academic year. Plan to major in a field of study leading to a profession in one of the following: Dental Medical Nursing Osteopathy Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent). PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: Albert Harris Scholarship
records.description: The Albert Harris Scholarship assists high school seniors who are attending Salem High School in Salem, NJ and plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Albert Harris Scholarship must be: High school seniors attending Salem High School in Salem, NJ Planning to enroll in full- or part-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. PNC Bank Employees, children of PNC Bank employees or Trust committee members are not eligible to apply.

records.title: BCU Scholarship Program
records.description: BCU has established a scholarship program to assist members who plan to continue their education in college, technical school, or in a certification program. Scholarships are offered each year for full-time study at an accredited institution of the student´s choice.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the BCU Scholarship Program must fulfill all the eligibility requirements. Student must be: A BCU member in good standing with your own account (not on parent’s account). Members of BCU also include members of GEICO Credit Union, Target Credit Union, UnitedHealth Group Credit Union, HCA Healthcare Credit Union and ADA Credit Union. It’s easy to join the Credit Union at time of application. Visit BCU.org and select “Join Today”. A high school (secondary school) senior or graduate, or current undergraduate student. Planning to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college or university, technical school, or certification program for the entire 2026-2027 academic year. Has not ever received any other scholarship Award of any type by BCU. BCU interns are eligible to apply. Children and/or Grandchildren of BCU employees are eligible to apply for specifically designated awards provided the employee/guardian is not a Vice President or higher.

records.title: LeRoy G. Erickson Memorial Scholarship Fund
records.description: The LeRoy G. Erickson Memorial Scholarship Fund was established to assist high school seniors at Bradford Area High School who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the LeRoy G. Erickson Memorial Program must: Be high school seniors from Bradford Area High School who plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college or university or vocational school for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale or the equivalent. PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: The Greatrex Scholarship Program
records.description: Because of the generosity and foresight of Elmer W. Greatrex, high school seniors and past recipients who are residents of Foxborough, Massachusetts, are eligible to apply for scholarship awards of $2,500.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to The Greatrex Scholarship Program must: Be high school seniors or past Greatrex scholarship recipients who are bona fide residents of Foxborough, Massachusetts, and Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two year or four year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Students must enroll in undergraduate study no later than the fall following their high school graduation.

records.title: Marguerite Lyons Scholarship Program
records.description: PNC Institutional Investments, Trustee, has established the Marguerite Lyons Scholarship to assist high school seniors from Kentucky who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Marguerite Lyons Scholarship Program must be: High school seniors residing in Kentucky. Planning to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Attending one of the following high schools: Boyd County High School, Ashland, KY Fairview High School, Ashland, KY Greenup County High School, Greenup, KY Lawrence County High School, Louisa, KY Paul G. Blazer High School, Ashland, KY Raceland-Worthington High School, Raceland, KY Rose Hill Christian School, Ashland, KY Russell High School, Russell, KY PNC Employees, children of PNC employees or Trust committee members are ineligible.

records.title: Charles E. Wolf Educational Trust
records.description: PNC Bank Trustee of the Charles E. Wolf Educational Trust has established a scholarship program to assist high school seniors in Kosciusko County and attend Warsaw Community High School, Tippecanoe Valley High School, Wawasee High School, Triton High School, or Whitko High School.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Charles E. Wolf Educational Trust must: Reside in Kosciusko County, Indiana at the time of application deadline Be a high school senior at Warsaw Community High School, Tippecanoe Valley High School, Wawasee High School, Triton High School, or Whitko High School Be a United States citizen Be an active member of a church Plan to enroll in fulltime undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: A. F. Robertson Family Memorial Fund
records.description: The A. F. Robertson Family Memorial Fund assists high school seniors who reside in Hamilton or Brownstown Township in Jackson County, Indiana and plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the A. F. Robertson Family Memorial Fund must be: Residents of Southern Indiana: first priority to residents of Brownstown and Hamilton Townships of Jackson County, Indiana, then to residents of southern Indiana. Planning to enroll in full-time study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: ZAFEE Scholarship Program
records.description: The Chicago Community Trust, as Trustee of the ZAFEE Foundation Fund, has established a scholarship program to assist current participants in Uniting Voices Chicago or recent refugees to the United States (within the last 5 years) who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the ZAFEE Scholarship Program must: Be current participants in Uniting Voices Chicago OR Be recent refugees to the United States (within the last 5 years) AND Be high school seniors who plan to enroll in part-time or full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year Have a minimum grade point average of 2.25 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) Dependents and immediate family members of donors and The Chicago Community Trust employees are ineligible .

records.title: Howard & Edna Postles Award
records.description: PNC Bank, N.A. Trustee of the PNC Bank Delaware (DE) Scholarships offers the Howard & Edna Postles Award for high school seniors who live within 15 miles of Milford, Delaware that plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Howard & Edna Postles Award must be: First-time applicants must be high school seniors who live within 15 miles of the Milford, DE city limits. Rank within the top 10% of their class academically. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate or graduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Undergraduates and graduate students who are previous recipients may reapply, but cannot receive more than eight (8) scholarships. PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply
records.award_amount: Awards to be determined by PNC Bank, N.A.

records.title: John H. Noll Scholarship
records.description: The John H. Noll Scholarship assists students who have graduated from high schools in the Fort Wayne, IN metropolitan area.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the John H. Noll Scholarship must be: High school seniors or graduates of public or parochial high schools in the Fort Wayne, IN metropolitan area. Enrolled or planning to enroll in full-time study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, vocational-technical or trade school for the entire upcoming academic year. Preference will be given to the average student (2.0 to 3.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale.) PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: J. Russell and Gladys Irene Carmell Scholarship
records.description: The J. Russell and Gladys Irene Carmell Scholarship assists U.S. citizens who have resided in the Tri-County, Michigan area and plan to pursue a nursing profession.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the J. Russell and Gladys Irene Carmell Scholarship must be: U.S. citizens who have resided in the Tri-County (Bay, Midland and Saginaw Counties, MI) area for a minimum of four years prior to scholarship application. High school seniors or the previous year graduates*, in the top 25% of their high school graduating class. Planning to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Planning to study and engage in a recognized nursing profession including Registered Nurse, Licensed Practical Nurse, or Nurse-Anesthetist. *The applicant should not have a gap of more than one year since commencement of high school. PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: Grant Munro Scholarship Program
records.description: The Grant Munro Scholarship assists students who have graduated from high schools in Fairfield County, OH and who are attending accredited undergraduate or graduate schools in medical or ministry fields.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Grant Munro Scholarship must be: High school seniors or graduates from high schools in Fairfield County, OH. Enrolled or planning to enroll in full-time study at an accredited undergraduate or graduate school for the entire upcoming academic year. Be majoring in medical or ministry fields. Students in the medical field must have a minimum cumulative 3.0 grade point average and be pursuing authorized medical titles. Students in the ministry field must have a minimum cumulative 3.0 grade point average and provide letter from sponsoring judicatory or local church-governing pastor. PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: Grahame and Thelma Somerville Scholarship Program
records.description: The Grahame and Thelma Somerville Scholarship assists non-traditional students who plan to attend an accredited undergraduate school.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Grahame and Thelma Somerville Scholarship must: Be a nontraditional student attending, or planning to attend, an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school in the United States for the entire upcoming academic year in an undergraduate course of study. Applicants from the state of Indiana are encouraged to apply. Have graduated from high school in the year 2021 or prior. Students may be enrolled part-time or full-time. PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: Gray Scholarship Fund
records.description: PNC Bank, N.A. as Trustee of the Gray Scholarship Fund has established a scholarship program to assist students in Massachusetts who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Gray Scholarship Fund must: Be high school seniors or graduates, or current postsecondary undergraduates from a high school in Massachusetts who plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Applicants from high schools in Middlesex County, Massachusetts are encouraged to apply. Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent). PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: Mauger Insurance Scholarship
records.description: The Mauger Insurance Scholarship has been established to assist students from Southwest Licking School District in Ohio who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Students who have previously received a Mauger Insurance Scholarship and wish to renew will receive an invitation to renew their scholarship in January 2026 and should not complete a new application. Applicants to the Mauger Insurance Scholarship must: Be a high school senior or graduate who has attended Southwest Licking School District for all four years of high school Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year Have a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5 on a 4.0 scale Recipient must demonstrate financial need. PNC Employees, children of PNC employees or Trust committee members are ineligible.

records.title: Dr. Joseph P. Pyle Award
records.description: PNC Bank, N.A. Trustee of the PNC Bank Delaware (DE) Scholarships offers the Dr. Joseph P. Pyle Award for high school seniors in Wilmington, DE planning to enroll in a college or vocational-technical program.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Dr. Joseph P. Pyle Award must: Be a high school senior residing in the city limits of Wilmington attending a high school within New Castle County or the City of Wilmington. Be between the ages of 17 and 21 year old a the time of application. Plan to enroll in full-time or part-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: William S. and Margaret I. Marvin Warroad Two-Year College Scholarship Program
records.description: The Marvin family has established a scholarship program for graduating Warroad High School seniors who exemplify the civic-mindedness of William S. and Margaret I. Marvin.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic William S. and Margaret I. Marvin Warroad Two-Year College Scholarship Program must: Be a graduating Warroad High School senior (class of 2026). Be enrolled full-time at Warroad High School during Junior and Senior year. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year college or vocational-technical school, or a university offering a two-year degree or certificate* for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 2.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent). *Certification programs must be through an accredited institution and must run on a standard academic semester calendar. Certification programs must be a minimum of one semester/term in length and applicants must be enrolled at the time awards are disbursed in July. Grandchildren, great-grandchildren, and great-great grandchildren of William S. and Margaret I. Marvin are ineligible.

records.title: Louis Ernst Family Scholarship
records.description: PNC Bank, N.A., Trustee has established the Louis Ernst Family Scholarship to assist high school seniors from Madison Consolidated High School and Shawe Memorial High School in Madison, Indiana who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Louis Ernst Family Scholarship must be: Graduating seniors from Madison Consolidated High School or Shawe Memorial High School in Madison, Indiana. Plan to enroll at an accredited two-year or four-year college or university or vocational-technical school. PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: The Hearn Educational Fund Award
records.description: PNC Bank, N.A. Trustee of the PNC Bank Delaware (DE) Scholarships offers the Hearn Educational Fund Award for high school seniors from Milford Senior High School who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to The Hearn Educational Fund Award must be: High school seniors graduating from Milford Senior High School. Residents within the boundaries of Milford, DE School District. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent). Undergraduates who are previous recipients may reapply PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: William J. McMannis and A. Haskell McMannis Educational Trust
records.description: The William J. McMannis and A. Haskell McMannis Educational Trust is being offered to assist students from Pennsylvania with their education. Up to 30 renewable scholarships ranging from an estimated $2,000 to $5,000 will be granted based on financial need.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the William J. McMannis and A. Haskell McMannis Educational Trust must: Be a Pennsylvania high school senior or graduate or current post-secondary undergraduate. Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent). Be a United States citizen. Plan to enroll in full-time study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Children of PNC Bank, N.A. employees are ineligible.

records.title: Ivy A. Monk Scholarship Trust Program
records.description: UMB Bank, Trustee of the Ivy A. Monk Scholarship has established a scholarship program to assist graduating high school seniors from designated high schools in Dickinson, Ottawa and Saline counties in Kansas who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs. Scholarships are offered each year for full-time study at an accredited institution of the student’s choice.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Ivy A. Monk Scholarship Trust Program must: Be a current high school senior at one of the following high schools in Dickinson, Ottawa, or Saline Counties in Kansas: Abilene Baptist Academy Abilene High School Ell-Saline High School Herington High School Hope High School Minneapolis High School Sacred Heart Jr.- Sr. High School Salina Central High School Salina South High School Solomon High School Southeast of Saline High School White City High School Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent).

records.title: Steve Stricker American Family Insurance Foundation Scholarship Program
records.description: Steve Stricker American Family Insurance Foundation (the Foundation) has established a scholarship program to assist students who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Steve Stricker American Family Insurance Foundation Scholarship Program must meet all of the following criteria: Be high school seniors graduating from a high school in Dane or Rock County, WI. Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Demonstrate engagement in the game of golf through one of these respective categories: competitive participation, recreational participation, employment at a golf course or golf retailer, caddy at a golf course, or volunteer at a golf tournament.

records.title: Merle E. and Olive Lee Gilliand Scholarship
records.description: The Merle E. and Olive Lee Gilliand Scholarship Program has been established to assist students at Duquesne University in Pittsburgh, PA. The sponsor will be PNC Bank in Pittsburgh, serving as Trustee of the M. Gilliand FBO Scholarship Foundation Trust and the Merle E. and Olive Lee Gilliand Scholarship Trust.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants must meet the following criteria: Be 26 years old or younger. Be current undergraduate students at Duquesne University. Be enrolled full-time for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum 3.0 grade point average on a 4.0 scale (or equivalent). Demonstrate financial need as calculated by Scholarship America.

records.title: Albert Francis Gilmartin Memorial Scholarship Program
records.description: The Boston Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist high school seniors at Quincy High School and North Quincy High School who plan to continue their education in undergraduate school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants must meet all of the following criteria Be residents of Quincy, MA or the Hough’s Neck neighborhood of Quincy, MA Be high school seniors attending North Quincy High School or Quincy High School Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited four-year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a cumulative grade point average of 3.0 or higher (4.0 scale) Demonstrate financial need.

records.title: Bernowski Scholarship Trust Fund
records.description: The Bernowski Scholarship Trust Fund assists students who are graduating seniors from Belle Vernon High School, Charleroi High School, or Ringgold High School in Pennsylvania and plan to continue their education at an accredited two- or four-year college or university in the 15000-16999 ZIP Code areas for the entire upcoming academic year.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Bernowski Scholarship Trust Fund must: Be high school seniors at one of the schools in Pennsylvania: Belle Vernon High School Charleroi High School Ringgold High School Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college or university in the 15000-16999 ZIP Code areas for the entire upcoming academic year PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: Stanley K. Powers Educational Trust Scholarship
records.description: The Stanley K. Powers Educational Trust Scholarship assists students from Allegheny County, Pennsylvania who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Stanley K. Powers Educational Trust Scholarship must: Be high school seniors or graduates, current undergraduates, or graduate level students Have a permanent address in Allegheny County, Pennsylvania Be enrolled or planning to enroll in full-time undergraduate or graduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: Laura M. Smedley Scholarship Fund
records.description: PNC Bank, N.A. offers the Laura M. Smedley Scholarship Fund to recognize residents of Venango County, PA who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Laura M. Smedley Scholarship Fund must: Be residents of Venango County, PA OR are graduates of high schools situated in Venango County. Are planning to attend or are attending accredited colleges/universities to obtain a two-year degree (not post-graduate studies) including the first two years of nursing educational courses at Clarion University, OR are planning to attend or are attending a four-year degree program at an accredited college/university in courses leading to a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent. Plan to enroll full-time in undergraduate study for the entire upcoming academic year as a freshman or sophomore. PNC Employees, or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: Teacher Voices Scholarship Program
records.description: Voya Financial has established a scholarship program, in partnership with the National Teacher of the Year Program, to recognize and support aspiring K-12 classroom teachers.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Teacher Voices Scholarship Program must meet all of the following criteria: Be high school seniors or graduates or current college undergraduates or graduate level students Plan to be an elementary or high school classroom teacher* Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate or graduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year Be the sole nominee of one of the 2025 State Teachers of the Year (“STOY”) in the 50 states, U.S. territories, DC, and the Department of Defense Education *High schools seniors and undergraduate students can have any major; however graduate students must be pursuing a degree in the education field or a related field.

records.title: San Clemente High School Math, Science, and Arts Scholarship Fund and The F. Dennis and Sharon Flynn Memorial Scholarship Fund
records.description: The San Clemente High School Math, Science, and Arts Scholarship Fund and the F. Dennis and Sharon Flynn Memorial Scholarship Fund were established to assist graduating high school seniors in pursuing a higher education.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the San Clemente High School Math, Science, Arts Scholarship Fund must meet all of the following criteria: Be a graduating high school senior from San Clemente High School. Plan to study and obtain a degree in a math, science (including medical-related fields), or arts-related major. Enrolled as a full-time student (minimum of 12 units) at an accredited four-year college or university. Applicants to the F. Dennis & Sharon Flynn Memorial Scholarship Fund must meet all of the following criteria: Be a graduating high school senior from San Clemente High School or Dana Hills High School. Study towards an undergraduate degree at a Catholic or Jesuit College or University.

records.title: Paul Hyland Harris Memorial Scholarships
records.description: The Paul Hyland Harris Memorial Scholarships assists seniors or graduates of high schools located in Crawford County, Venango County, or Warren County in Pennsylvania. Students must be planning to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at Allegheny College or Harvard University.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Paul Hyland Harris Memorial Scholarships must: Be seniors or graduates of a high school located in Crawford County, Venango County, or Warren County in Pennsylvania. Be planning to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at Allegheny College or Harvard University for the entire upcoming academic year. Children of the Paul Hyland Harris Memorial Scholarships Trust, PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: John K. Henne Scholarship Foundation
records.description: PNC Bank, N.A., as trustee of the John K. Henne Scholarship Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist high school seniors or graduates of Titusville Area High School who plan to continue their education in college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the John K. Henne Scholarship Foundation must meet all of the following criteria: Be high school seniors or graduates of Titusville Area High School in Titusville, PA. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited four-year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year. Children of the John K. Henne family, PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: David and Pauline Gregory Trust Fund
records.description: The David and Pauline Gregory Trust Fund has established a scholarship program to assist high school seniors or high school graduates from the Titusville Area School District, Pennsylvania who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the David and Pauline Gregory Trust Fund must: Be current high school seniors or high school graduates from the Titusville Area School District, Pennsylvania pursuing undergraduate or graduate degrees. Demonstrate financial need and exemplary merit and character. Plan to enroll full-time in an accredited two- or four-year college or university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: Siebenthal and Block Scholarship Program
records.description: The Siebenthal and Block Scholarship Program has been established to assist students who attended Peoria Manual High School in Peoria, Illinois and plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Siebenthal and Block Scholarship Program must: Be high school seniors or graduates, or current college undergraduates, who attended Peoria Manual High School in Peoria, IL. Plan to enroll in fulltime undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year PNC employees or Trust committee members, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: Mike Groff Community Leader Award
records.description: Toyota has established a scholarship program to assist graduate level students working towards a Master’s or Ph.D. in any discipline. Scholarships are offered each year for full- or part-time study at an accredited four-year college or university of the student’s choice.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Mike Groff Community Leader Award must be: Nominated by one of the Toyota partnered Boys & Girls Clubs in California. Each nonprofit partner may only nominate one student per year. Graduate level students working towards a Master’s or Ph.D. in any discipline Planning to enroll in full- or part-time graduate level study at an accredited four-year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year Employees, vendors and business partners of Toyota and its parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, promotion and advertising agencies, and members of their immediate family (defined as spouse and parent, children and siblings and their respective spouses, regardless of where they reside) and persons living in the same household, whether or not related, of such employees, are not eligible to apply. Students may not be recipients of both the Mike Groff Community Leader Award and the Toyota Scholarship during the same academic year.

records.title: Samuel Epstein Foundation Fund
records.description: The Samuel Epstein Foundation Trust has established a scholarship program to assist graduating high school seniors at Warren High School, Warren, PA who plan to continue their education in college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Samuel Epstein Foundation Fund must: Be graduating high school seniors at Warren High School, Warren, PA who have attended Warren High School for at least two years prior to graduation. Be enrolled or plan to enrolled at a two- or four-year college or university in the United States for the entire upcoming academic year. PNC Employees, children of PNC employees or Trust committee members are ineligible. Due to the closing of Sheffield High School and students now attending Warren High School there is ongoing legal process to update the requirements and governing language of the scholarship. Warren High School students who previously attended Sheffield Area High School are eligible to apply Warren County High School seniors that live in the East Attendance Area are eligible to apply

records.title: Technical Education for Energized Careers Scholarship
