records.title: The George Foundation Higher Education Scholarship Program
records.description: The George Foundation has established a scholarship program for high school seniors and undergraduate students residing in Fort Bend County, Texas.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the The George Foundation Higher Education Scholarship Program must be: Residing in Fort Bend County, Texas . U.S. citizens or U.S. permanent residents or have been granted deferred action status under the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals Program (DACA)*. Graduating High school seniors or undergraduates who plan to enroll or who are already in a full-time (minimum 12 credit hours) undergraduate course of study at an accredited two- or four-year public college or university in Texas. Have a minimum GPA of 2.5 or higher on a 4.0 scale. Demonstrate a financial need. *Non-U.S. citizen applicants are required to be U.S. permanent residents and must submit a copy of their U.S. permanent resident card with their application. Student visas are not acceptable. DACA students must submit their approval letter. Awards are for undergraduate study only.

records.title: American Family Insurance Dreams Foundation Scholarship Program
records.description: American Family Insurance Dreams Foundation, Inc. has established scholarship programs to assist dependents of full-time American Family Insurance employees, American Family Insurance agency owners or American Family Insurance agency staff who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the American Family Insurance Dreams Foundation Scholarship Program must meet all of the following criteria: Be dependent* children of full-time American Family Insurance, Homesite/Connect Auto and Home employees, Main Street America, AFICS, agents, and agency staff** who have at least one (1) year of employment with the company as of the application deadline. Applicants who have received a scholarship from this Program prior to the start of this current Program cycle shall not be required to meet eligibility requirements concerning any employment with the Sponsor. *Dependent children are defined as a biological, step- or legally adopted children or grandchildren living in the employee’s household or primarily supported by the employee. **Dependents of agency staff must include a letter from the employing agent. Be high school seniors graduating in 2026. Be enrolled in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale, or its equivalent. Dependents of Foundation officers, Board of Directors, or Vice Presidents and above, are ineligible to apply.

records.title: Fairfield County’s Community Foundation Competitive Scholarship Program
records.description: Fairfield County’s Community Foundation has established a scholarship program for high school and college students from Fairfield County.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Graduating high school senior applicants to the Fairfield County’s Community Foundation Competitive Scholarship Program must: Be a graduating senior from any high school in Fairfield County. Be in good academic standing (generally a cumulative GPA of 2.7 or better on a 4.0 scale or the equivalent unless specified by specific fund). Demonstrate financial need. Plan to attend an accredited two-year or four-year college or university or post-high school vocational training unless specified by specific fund. Students may be enrolling in either full-time or part-time study unless specified by the specific fund. Current undergraduate or graduate applicants to the Fairfield County’s Community Foundation Competitive Scholarship Program must: Be a current undergraduate (NOT an incoming freshman) or graduate student enrolled in a program at an accredited college, university or vocational school, or specialized study program Have a connection, as a native resident, high school graduate, or current resident of Fairfield County. NOTE: This criterion does not apply for students enrolled at Sacred Heart University applying for the Megan Cobb & Jason Kern Scholarship. Demonstrate financial need. Demonstrate a history of academic achievement (generally a minimum cumulative 2.7 GPA on a 4.0 scale or the equivalent unless specified by specific fund) Students may be enrolling full-time or part-time unless specified by the specific fund. Awards may be used for graduate or undergraduate study unless specified by the specific fund. The program consists of many separate scholarship funds administered by Fairfield County’s Community Foundation. Some funds have additional eligibility requirements as noted below.

records.title: Elam Baer and Janis Clay Epilepsy Scholarship
records.description: This scholarship was created to support students who live in Minnesota, North Dakota, South Dakota, Wisconsin, or Iowa and have shown courage in dealing with epilepsy, commitment to their education, and perseverance in eliminating the obstacles that epilepsy may present. Selection is based on how the applicant has navigated challenges due to epilepsy, their career goals, achievements, etc.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Elam Baer and Janis Clay Scholarship must: Reside in Minnesota, North Dakota, South Dakota, Wisconsin, or Iowa. Have an epilepsy or seizure diagnosis. Be high school seniors, graduates, current college undergraduates, or graduate students. Plan to enroll in part-time or full-time undergraduate or graduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school during the upcoming academic year.* Have a minimum grade point average of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent). *Certification programs must be through an accredited institution. Certification programs must be a minimum of one semester/term in length and recipients must be enrolled at the time awards are disbursed. wysiwyg_basic

records.title: Tencent America Scholarship
records.description: The Tencent America Scholarship aims to provide financial support for high school seniors who are pursuing a video game-related major.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Tencent America Scholarship must: Be a United States citizen or permanent resident Be graduating high school seniors (Class of 2026) Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) Study a video game-related major and aspire for a career in the gaming industry. Video game-related majors include but are not limited to: Game Development & Design: Game Development / Game Programming / Game Production / Game Design / Interactive Media / Digital Production / Real-Time Interactive Simulation (RTIS) Art, Animation & Storytelling: Music and Sound Design / Audio Engineering / Animation / Computer Graphics / Creative Writing / Narrative Design / 3D Modeling / Visual Effects (VFX) / Graphic Design / Motion Design Technology & Data: Computer Science / Software Engineering / Data Science / Data Analytics / UX/UI Design / Quality Assurance (QA) Employees of Tencent America, LLC and their children are ineligible to apply.

records.title: New York Life Golden Futures Scholarship
records.description: The New York Life Golden Futures Scholarship identifies and awards outstanding high school students who have completed specified New York Life Golden Futures Scholarship game modules.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the New York Life Golden Futures Scholarship must: Be a current high school junior * or senior, who is a legal resident of the 50 United States or the District of Columbia. Complete the required number of levels of the New York Life Golden Futures game. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college/university or vocational-technical or trade school for the entire upcoming academic year (or following year for juniors). Fulfill any other eligibility requirements set forth in the New York Life Golden Futures Scholarship Official Rules. Children of employees and agents of New York Life and Supplier are ineligible. * High school juniors who are selected as recipients will have their award deferred for one year and will receive their award upon high school graduation and enrollment for that upcoming academic year. Students must have completed their junior or senior year to be eligible to apply.

records.description: Brave of Heart Nursing Scholarship seeks to identify and award America’s future leaders in nursing.

Plan to enroll in full-time or part-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college or university for the 2026-27 academic year (Fall and/or Spring semesters). Have a minimum grade point average of 2.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent). Be in good standing according to school policy. Demonstrate financial need.

records.title: AbbVie Immunology Scholarship
records.description: A scholarship for exceptional students living with chronic inflammatory diseases.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic It is not necessary for applicants to have taken, currently take, or intend to take in the future any medicine or product marketed by AbbVie; this will not be a consideration in the recipient-selection process. AbbVie Immunology Scholarship applicants must be: A US citizen or a legal and permanent resident of the US Diagnosed with AD, AS, CD, GCA, HS, JIA, jPsA, Ps, PsA, RA, UC, or UV by a healthcare professional. records.title: TIAA First-Generation Scholarship
records.description: TIAA has established a scholarship program to assist first-generation undergraduate students who plan to continue their education in college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the TIAA First-Generation Scholarship Program must: Be first-generation* students *For the purpose of this scholarship program, “first-generation” is defined as neither parent/guardian of the student having previously received a 4-year college/university degree Be current college undergraduates Plan to continue in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited four-year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year Pursue a career related to Financial Services or Asset Management, including examples such as Business, Marketing, Human Resources, Legal, Information Technology, etc. Have a minimum grade point average of 2.8 or higher on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent) Be United States citizens Past recipients of the Nuveen Invest in the Future Scholarship are NOT eligible.

records.title: CopperPoint Insurance Companies Community Scholarship Program
records.description: Assisting current undergraduate sophomores and juniors, who currently reside in or attend school in Alaska, Arizona, California, Idaho, or Washington.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the CopperPoint Insurance Companies Community Scholarship must: Be a current college undergraduate in sophomore or junior year who will be enrolled in the 2026-27 academic year as a junior or senior Be planning to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited four-year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year Be a resident of or be attending school in one of the following states: Alaska Arizona California Idaho Washington CopperPoint Insurance Companies’ current or previous employees and their dependents are ineligible.

records.title: J.W. Pepper 150th Anniversary Scholarship
records.description: J.W. Pepper & Son, Inc. has established a scholarship program to assist students who plan to continue their education in college while pursuing a music education degree.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the J.W. Pepper 150th Anniversary Scholarship Program must: Be high school seniors or graduates who are entering their first full year of college/university*. *Students who have taken college courses or enrolled in Postsecondary Enrollment Options (PSEO) during high school are eligible to apply. Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited four-year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year. Plan to enroll in a music education degree program. Be a current or former member, in good standing, of one of your high school music programs (Band, Orchestra, or Choir). Children of JW Pepper & Son, Inc. employees are ineligible to apply.

records.title: Marion E. McRae Trust Forestry Scholarship
records.description: The Midland Trust Company, trustee of Marion E. McRae Trust has established a scholarship program to assist New Jersey residents who plan to continue their education in college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Marion E. McRae Trust Forestry Scholarship must: Be a resident of New Jersey studying a major related to Forestry* High school seniors or graduates, or current postsecondary undergraduates Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year Have a minimum grade point average of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent). Midland Trust employees and children of Midland Trust employees are ineligible. *Approved majors include: Forestry: (General) Forest Management/Natural Resource Management Forestry: (other specialized tracks) Technology Integration: (GIS, remote sensing, AI, and drones) Sustainable Forest Management: Emphasis on climate-smart forestry, carbon accounting, and ecosystem services Wildfire Prevention and Management Urban Forestry Environmental Policy & Guidance Forestry/Environmental/Mechanical Engineering Wildlife Ecology/Biology Conservation Management Other: industries related to forestry

records.title: DLA Piper Scholarship Programs
records.description: DLA Piper is offering two scholarship opportunities up to $6,000 each for those interested in pursuing a law degree: LEAP (Legal Elite Athlete Pipeline) for student athletes BRAVO (Building Relationships to Advance Veterans’ Opportunities) for veterans
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Legal Elite Athlete Pipeline (LEAP) and Building Relationships to Advance Veterans’ Opportunities (BRAVO) Scholarships must meet the eligibility requirements for whichever scholarship award they are applying for. LEAP (Legal Elite Athlete Pipeline) Scholarship Program LEAP applicants must meet all of the following criteria: Be 18 years old or the age of majority in their state of residence (whichever is greater) Be interested in pursuing a legal degree on a part-time or full-time basis Have completed at least two years of undergraduate study at an accredited United States college or university Have a minimum of a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale Have participated in at least two (2) years in a competitive intercollegiate athletic program offered by an accredited United States college or university Plan to enroll in an LSAT prep course or apply to an accredited law school within one year of finishing the scholarship program BRAVO (Building Relationships to Advance Veterans’ Opportunities) Scholarship Program BRAVO applicants must meet all of the following criteria: Be 18 years old or the age of majority in their state of residence (whichever is greater) Be enrolled or have graduated from an accredited United States college or university on a part-time or full-time basis Have a minimum of a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale Have served in the United States military, this includes the Reserves and National Guard, and be honorably discharged (no longer drilling or serving) veterans who have received a Certificate of Eligibility from the Department of Veterans Affairs or DD214 or another document of service stating “Honorable Discharged” by the program start date Plan to enroll in an LSAT prep course or apply to an accredited law school within one year of finishing the scholarship program
records.award_amount: $1,000 for LSAT prep and application fees and $5,000 for Law School

records.title: William C. and Corrine J. Dietrich Scholarship Program
records.description: The William C. and Corinne J. Dietrich Scholarship Program has been established for current high school seniors who plan to continue their education an accredited two-year or four-year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year. Four awards will be allocated to current high school seniors of Le Sueur- Henderson High School in Le Sueur, MN or Maple River High School in Mapleton, MN or other such public high schools serving Le Sueur or Mapleton. Depending on remaining funds, additional competitive awards are open to current high school seniors attending any public high school in Minnesota.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Merit award recipients must meet all of the following criteria: Be current high school seniors of Le Sueur- Henderson High School in Le Sueur, MN or Maple River High School in Mapleton, MN or other such public high schools serving Le Sueur or Mapleton. Be the outstanding scholastic achiever in the graduating class named by Le Sueur- Henderson High School and Maple River High School as the top ranked students in their respective high schools. Plan to enroll in full‑time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four‑year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year. Competitive award applicants must meet the following criteria: Be current high school seniors of Le Sueur- Henderson High School in Le Sueur, MN or Maple River High School in Mapleton, MN or other such public high schools serving Le Sueur or Mapleton. Two awards are earmarked for these schools. Be current high school seniors attending a public high school in Minnesota. The number of competitive awards will be determined according to funds remaining for distribution after allocation of funds for William C. Dietrich awards and Connie Borchert Dietrich awards. Demonstrate financial need. Plan to enroll in full‑time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four‑year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year.

records.title: William A. March Education Trust Scholarship
records.description: PNC Bank, N.A. offers the William A. March Education Trust Scholarship to assist students who plan to continue their education in college or graduate school.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the William A. March Education Trust Scholarship must: Be high school seniors, high school graduates, current college undergraduates or graduate students Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate or graduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university, vocational-technical school or graduate school for the entire upcoming academic year PNC employees, their immediate family members, and members of their households are not eligible to apply.

records.title: Western Digital STEM Scholarship
records.description: Western Digital’s STEM scholarship program is designed to support the next generation of talent as they work toward their career goals.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the U.S. Western Digital STEM Scholarship must meeting the following criteria: Important Eligibility Information, Please Read Carefully Be a current full-time undergraduate student attending a two-year community college in the United States (U.S.) Planning to transfer to full-time enrollment at an accredited four-year college or university in the U.S. for the upcoming academic year (for which the scholarship will be applied) Pursuing a Bachelor of Science Degree in the field of Mathematics, Engineering, Computer Science, or other Sciences (not including agricultural, health, or life) Have a minimum GPA of 2.7 on a 4.0 scale (or equivalent) Demonstrate financial need or hardship Please Note: Only applicants meeting all criteria will be considered. Only submit an application if you are currently enrolled in a two-year community college and plan to transfer to a four-year college or university in the upcoming academic year. Students who have received two Western Digital Scholarships in the past are ineligible. Dependents of Western Digital employees who meet the requirements are eligible to apply. However, preference will not be given to employee dependents.

records.title: Wells Fargo Veterans Scholarship Program
records.description: Wells Fargo is strongly invested in supporting our nation’s veterans, including a commitment to assist them in completing postsecondary education programs to help them return to, and succeed in, a competitive job market.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Wells Fargo Veterans Scholarship Program must: Have served in the United States military, this includes the Reserves and National Guard. Be honorably-discharged by the application deadline date (no longer drilling or serving) veterans who have received a Certificate of Eligibility from the Department of Veterans Affairs or DD214 or another document of service stating “Honorable Discharged” by the program application deadline date. A spouse or widowed person of disabled veterans meeting the above criteria may also apply. Be high school or GED graduates, current undergraduate or graduate level one students enrolled in full-time undergraduate (first Associates or Bachelor’s) or graduate (first Master’s degree) study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school* for the entire upcoming academic year. Doctorate study is not eligible. *College must not be on warning or probationary status with the federal government, or must not be in litigation with the federal government or a state. Have completed the FAFSA to ensure full discovery of actual unmet need. Use any military education benefits for which they are eligible in the upcoming academic year. Have a minimum cumulative grade point average of 2.0 on a 4.0 scale, or its equivalent.

records.title: Wells Fargo Veterans Emergency Grant Program
records.description: The Wells Fargo Veterans Emergency Grants are designed to help U.S. military veterans who are pursuing a postsecondary degree and who face financial emergencies that impact their ability to pay for school.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Wells Fargo Veterans Emergency Grant Program must: Have served in the United States military, this includes the Reserves and National Guard. Be honorably-discharged (no longer drilling or serving) veterans who have received a Certificate of Eligibility from the Department of Veterans Affairs or DD214 or another document of service stating “Honorable Discharged” by the program application deadline date. Spouses or widowed person of disabled veterans meeting the above criteria may also apply. Be high school or GED graduates, current undergraduate or graduate level one students enrolled in full-time undergraduate (first Associates or Bachelor’s) or graduate (first Master’s degree) study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school* for the entire upcoming academic year. Doctorate study is not eligible. Have completed the FAFSA to ensure full discovery of actual unmet need. Use any military education benefits for which they are eligible in the upcoming academic year. Have a minimum cumulative grade point average of 2.0 on a 4.0 scale, or its equivalent. *College must not be on warning or probationary status with the federal government, or must not be in litigation with the federal government or a state. Previous recipients are not eligible.

records.title: Wells Fargo Stacey Milbern Scholarship
records.description: The Wells Fargo Stacey Milbern Scholarship is designed to help students with disabilities pursue the education or training they need to succeed in their chosen career path.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants of the Wells Fargo Stacey Milbern Scholarship award must: Have an identified disability (defined as someone who has, or considers themselves to have, a long-term or recurring issue that impacts one or more major life activity). Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale or its equivalent. Be a high school senior or graduate or a current postsecondary undergraduate who plans to enroll or who is already enrolled in full-time or half-time (at least 6 credits per term) undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college or university in the United States for the entire upcoming academic year. Be a US citizen or legal resident currently residing in the USA. Note: Only the first 700 completed applications received will be considered.

records.title: Scholarship America Veteran Scholarship for Educators
records.description: The Scholarship America Veteran Scholarship for Educators supports U.S. Armed Forces veterans who plan to continue serving their communities by pursuing careers in the K-12 school system.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic To apply for the Scholarship America Veteran Scholarship for Educators, applicants must meet the following requirements: Have served in the United States military, to include the Reserves, National Guard and Coast Guard. Be an honorably discharged veteran, no longer drilling or serving by July 2027. Provide one of the following documents before award disbursement: Certificate or Letter of Eligibility from the Department of Veteran Affairs. DD214 or other document proving honorable service. Be pursuing a degree or state-approved certificate in education or school-based counseling, school-based social worker, or school psychology, with the intent to work in the K-12 school system. Be a high school or GED graduate, current post-secondary undergraduate, or graduate-level student. Plan to enroll in one of the following: Full- or part-time study in an undergraduate or graduate program leading to an associate’s, bachelor’s, or master’s degree at an accredited two- or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Doctoral programs are not eligible. A state-approved alternative pathway to certification. Attend a college or institution that: Is not on warning or probationary status with the federal government. Is not in litigation with the federal or a state government. Maintain a minimum GPA of 2.0 on a 4.0 scale (or equivalent).

records.title: The Vertex Foundation Scholarship
records.description: A scholarship for students affected by cystic fibrosis (CF) and their immediate family members or caregivers.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Vertex Foundation Scholarship Program must: Be a United States or Canadian citizen or a foreign national lawfully admitted to the United States or Canada for permanent residence Be high school seniors/students in their final year of upper or higher secondary school, high school/upper or higher secondary school graduates, current technical or college/university undergraduate, and graduate level students in good academic standing Plan to enroll in part-time or full-time undergraduate or graduate study at an accredited two-, three- or four-year college or university, CEGEP institution (or equivalent) in the United States or Canada for the entire upcoming academic year Consent to disclose any information you provide with Scholarship America, Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated, the Vertex Foundation, and the academic institution Be diagnosed with cystic fibrosis OR Be an immediate* family member of an individual who has been diagnosed with cystic fibrosis *Immediate family members are defined as siblings, caregivers, children or spouses. Vertex Pharmaceuticals and Vertex Foundation employees, contractors, former employees, employee dependents and immediate family members are ineligible.

records.title: Health Care Scholars United
records.description: Are you a current or aspiring health professional? This $3,200 scholarship will help you take your healthcare career to the next level.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Let’s see if you’re eligible: Pursuing clinical health careers upon graduation Applicants must be pursuing a certification or degree in a clinical health career. Priority will be given to students seeking careers in pharmacy, rural health, behavioral health, maternal health, or primary care. 2026-2027 Enrollment Applicants must be enrolled as a full or part-time undergraduate or graduate student or plan to be enrolled in an accredited program at the time of award distribution (November 2026). Applicants must be enrolled in either an in-person or virtual program that is based in the United States. Program completion Applicants must be on track to graduate or complete their program no later than August 31, 2027. Applicants with anticipated graduation dates beyond August 31, 2027 are encouraged to apply for the next application cycle, which is scheduled to open in early 2027. Click the “Remind Me” button to receive updates when the next cycle opens. Demonstration of financial need Applicants must demonstrate financial need upon application. U.S. citizens Applicants must be U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, or lawful permanent residents. Certification programs must be through an accredited institution and must run on a standard academic semester calendar. Certification programs must be a minimum of one semester/term in length and applicants must be enrolled at the time awards are disbursed. Awards can be used for license programs and will be made payable to the accredited college, university, or vocational-technical school. Awards cannot be used for license fees or exams. Examples include but are not limited to: nursing, physician assistant, clinical psychologist, or clinical social worker. Current physicians who are seeking additional certifications or degrees are not eligible for this scholarship. Previous United Health Foundation scholarship recipients are not eligible for this scholarship. Employees of UnitedHealth Group, UnitedHealthcare, Optum, or an organization acquired by UnitedHealth Group, and their immediate family members are not eligible for this scholarship.

records.title: Tampa Bay Buccaneers She is Football Scholarship
records.description: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist female high school seniors participating in a form of football (touch, flag, tackle, etc.) who plan to continue their education in college.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers She is Football Scholarship must: Be female high school seniors participating in a form of football (touch, flag, tackle, etc). Plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited four-year college or university for the entire upcoming academic year. Have a minimum grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent). Write an essay (2,000 characters or less) on what qualities or traits you’ve learned from playing sports and how you plan on applying those both in college and throughout your career.

records.title: Steiner Family Scholarship
records.description: Students in the U.S and Canada are invited to apply for renewable scholarships of up to $5,000 (USD) per year through the Steiner Family Scholarship Program.

records.title: SNC STEM Scholarship
records.description: SNC’s mission is to safeguard our freedom and inspire the next generation to make a lasting impact through technology and imagination. The SNC STEM scholarship aims to support and empower students pursuing degrees in STEM-related fields.

records.title: SMART Scholarship Program
records.description: SMART offers merit-based, full-tuition STEM scholarships for undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral students pursuing degrees in one of the SMART STEM disciplines.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic SMART Scholarship applicants must: Be a citizen of the United States, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, or United Kingdom Have and maintain a cumulative GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale Be currently pursuing, or intend to pursue in fall 2027, a bachelor’s, master’s, or doctoral degree in a SMART STEM discipline Plan to attend, or enrolled in, a regionally accredited U.S. college or university* Be able to obtain and maintain a security clearance** Be requesting between 1-5 years of degree funding. Degree funding will start in August 2027 Complete summer internships for awards greater than 1.5 years Accept a one-for-one post-graduation service commitment as a civilian employee of the Department of War *High school seniors and incoming college freshmen who will be pursuing a bachelor’s degree in fall 2027 are eligible to apply. **Security clearances are initiated by a scholar’s Sponsoring Facility after award.

records.title: Scholarship America Dream Award
records.description: Scholarship America has established a scholarship program to help students currently enrolled in higher education programs (two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school).

records.title: Frontline Families Scholarship
records.description: A scholarship for educational assistance to the surviving children of frontline healthcare workers who lost their lives in the fight against COVID-19.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Frontline Families Scholarship Program must be: A child of a deceased frontline healthcare worker who died from COVID-19 while employed at a medical facility. High school seniors, high school graduates, or current college undergraduates. Planning to enroll in full-time or part-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Children are defined as biological, step- or legally adopted children age 26 and under as of the application date. Frontline healthcare workers are defined as the following occupations: nurse, physician, diagnosing clinician, health care support, medical first responder, healthcare technologist, community or social worker, administrator/administrative support, security personnel, cleaner, culinary/food service, coroner, and pharmacist. Ineligible occupations include non-medical frontline workers, such as supermarket employees, delivery workers, ride-share drivers or funeral home staff. Other occupations will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

records.title: The Families of Freedom Scholarship Fund
records.description: The Families of Freedom Scholarship Fund supports financially needy dependent children, spouses, and domestic partners of 9/11 victims. The Families of Freedom Scholarship Fund will end in 2030.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Registrants must be dependent children, spouses, or domestic partners of 9/11 victims, including airplane crew and passengers; World Trade Center and Pentagon workers and visitors; and relief workers, including firefighters, emergency medical personnel, and law enforcement personnel, who were involved in the rescue efforts. Parents and siblings of victims are not eligible unless they can provide documentation of financial dependence on the victim. All scholarship applicants must complete the registration process prior to submitting their first application. The Families of Freedom Scholarship Fund is only accepting registrations for victims who passed away on the day of September 11, 2001. Registration for the families of disabled victims is closed. Families of Freedom Scholarships are available for children who enroll in a program of postsecondary study by age 24. (Those children who turn 24 during their course of study must then continue their program of study uninterrupted, with the exception of summer vacations, in order to continue receiving scholarship assistance.) The Families of Freedom Scholarship is a need-based award. Students who show no financial need may receive a modest onetime award of up to $1,000*. They will not qualify for additional funding (unless their financial situation changes). Students are encouraged to reapply each year to see if they qualify. *Student eligible for the Twin Towers Award will still qualify to receive Twin Towers funding even if they do not qualify to receive the Families of Freedom Award. Twin Towers recipients must still apply for the Families of Freedom Scholarship to receive their award. Permanently Disabled Permanently disabled individuals must be deemed disabled by the Social Security Administration and have successfully completed the Families of Freedom registration process prior to September 30, 2016. The registration period has closed indefinitely for victims who were permanently disabled as a direct result of 9/11. Children of disabled registrants must have been born after September 11, 2001 but prior to September 30, 2008 in order to be eligible. Eligible Uses of Funds Scholarships may be used to attend an accredited vocational-technical school, trade school, two-year college, four-year college, or university located in the United States. Funds are only available for undergraduate study. Families of Freedom Scholarships are available for postsecondary study only. The Families of Freedom Scholarship Fund does not provide scholarships for elementary or secondary school. Families of Freedom Scholarship recipients may receive need-based scholarship awards for up to four years, or the equivalent if attendance is part-time, depending on total funding available. Eligibility for scholarship assistance is always based on financial need, as calculated by our financial need formula. Families of Freedom Scholarships are not provided to pay tuition or student loans retroactively. Although conditions may change over time, including the percentage of financial need covered, retroactive payments will not be made from the Fund to past recipients. Staying Eligible Grades are not considered in determining initial eligibility for Families of Freedom scholarships or the value of scholarship awards. However, a transcript of grades is required to verify enrollment and course completion for prior terms. Students must apply each year for awards from the Fund in order to determine continued eligibility and award amount. Eligibility for scholarship assistance is always based on financial need. Award amounts for eligible students may change yearly, based on changes in family finances, changes in tuition rates, and current actuarial projections for the Fund. Application Periods Applications must be submitted within the periods listed below. Late applications will not be accepted. 2026-2027 Full-Year: May 5, 2026 – August 5, 2026 Fall 2026 Term: August 15, 2026 – October 15, 2026 Spring 2027 Term: December 15, 2026 – February 15, 2027

records.title: Scholarship America Essential Visionaries Fund
records.description: The Essential Visionaries Scholarship Fund offers renewable scholarships to students pursuing degrees or certificates in education, counseling, psychology, or nursing through college or vocational school programs. This program is dedicated to empowering future professionals committed to making a meaningful impact, particularly within K-12 school systems and healthcare fields.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Essential Visionaries Scholarship Fund must meet the following criteria: Be high school seniors, high school graduates, GED graduates, or current college undergraduates residing in the United States (U.S.). Plan to enroll in part-time or full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college or university or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. Attend a college or institution that: Is not on warning or probationary status with the federal government. Is not in litigation with the federal or a state government. Be pursuing a degree or certificate* with a major in Education, Counseling, Social Work, Psychology, or Pre-Nursing/Nursing. Applicants pursuing education, counseling, social work, or psychology must demonstrate a commitment to working within the K-12 system. Nursing applicants are not required to demonstrate K-12 system involvement. Have a minimum grade point average of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent). Additional Notes: *Certification programs must be through an accredited institution, follow a standard academic semester calendar, and be a minimum of one semester/term in length. If you change your course of study from education, counseling, social work, psychology, or nursing/pre-nursing, you may become ineligible for this scholarship program. Applicants must be enrolled in an eligible program at the time awards are disbursed in August. Individuals granted deferred action status under the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals Program (DACA) are eligible and are encouraged to apply.

Please visit https://www.credithuman.com/join-credit-human to learn more about becoming a member. Children, grandchildren, or spouses of Credit Human employees are eligible to apply. Credit Human employees are not eligible. High school seniors (including seniors who will graduate with an associate’s degree as part of a dual enrollment program) and students attending trade, technical or vocational-technical schools, independent programs, and/or internship opportunities are not eligible.

records.title: Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship
records.description: The Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship program is providing high school seniors with an opportunity to upgrade their careers with a scholarship of up to $40,000, plus internship opportunities at Amazon!
records.eligibility: Let’s see if you’re eligible: special_list icons white university You’re planning to pursue a computer science degree in college, here are the majors we accept Planning to pursue a bachelor’s degree in computer science or other computer science related field of study and are planning to attend an accredited 4-year college or university in the United States (or an accredited 2-year college, with the intent to transfer to a 4-year institution). Majors Computer Science Computer Engineering Software Engineering Computer Programming Math (Mathematics; Applied Math) Data Science Electrical Engineering Transportation Technology Computer Info Systems Computer Info Science Cognitive Science Informatics Information Technologies atom You have experience in computer science or experience in tech To qualify, you need to have taken computer science classes in high school or at a college dual program, or currently be enrolled in one. Examples include: AP Computer Science A AP Computer Science Principles Computer Programming Computer Science Principles IB Computer Science Java Programming PLTW Computer Science Essentials It’s cool if you have not! You can take a qualifying exam offered by Amazon. usd-circle You’ve got a financial gap to fill This opportunity is offered to support students with a substantial need for financial assistance. If that hits home, this is for you. book-open You’re a high school senior with a 2.3 cumulative GPA Students need a minimum 2.3 GPA (on a 4.0 scale or equivalent) and a commitment to their studies. desktop Work Eligible in the United States for at least two years This includes United States citizens, United States permanent residents (holders of a Permanent Resident Card), or Employment Authorized to work in the United States. Employment authorization must be valid for at least 2 years. wysiwyg_basic How are recipients chosen? Amazon Future Engineer Scholarship empowers the next generation of tech innovators. As a high school senior, you can launch your tech career with this opportunity. Turn your passion for tech into your future. We use a holistic selection process that considers numerous criteria and materials you provide to choose winners across the nation. This includes things like: How you do in the classroom, primarily based on GPA Real-world experience – Including coding clubs, after- school clubs, self-taught projects, hackathons and related activities Work experience Short answer responses Financial need – Usually based on household income When you submit your application, we’ll look at all these areas to get a full picture of your fit for this scholarship. special_list icons tan What docs do I need? See below for a full checklist of required documents. In order to make your application complete, make sure everything is uploaded electronically by the deadline of January 26, 2026 at 3 PM CT. check-circle Online Recommendation We’d prefer this to be your computer science teacher if you have one, or a teacher who knows you well check-circle Transcript of Grades Transcripts should be from schools you have attended and/or are currently attending. Documents should display student name, school name, grades and credit hours for each course, and term when each course was taken. check-circle Most Recently Filed 1040 Include a copy of the first two pages of your household’s most recently filed IRS 1040 form(s) used for the Financial Information Page. If you are being claimed as a dependent on another person’s IRS 1040 tax return, you must submit the first two pages of that particular tax return with the application. Note: Please black out any sensitive data including Social Security Numbers before uploading.

records.title: Ancestry’s HistoryMakers Scholarship
records.description: To help support the next generation of change-makers, Ancestry launched the HistoryMakers Scholarship in 2022. Administered by Scholarship America, it’s designed for students who are just as passionate about where we come from as where we’re headed.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Applicants to the Ancestry’s HistoryMakers Scholarship Program must: Be a high school senior/high school graduate (entering undergraduate study Fall 2025), current college undergraduate or graduate student Be enrolled in full-time undergraduate or graduate study at one of the following United States (U.S.) or United Kingdom (U.K.) universities from Fall 2025 semester through Spring 2026 semester: United States Universities Bowie State University (U.S.) California State University, Sacramento (U.S.) Florida International University (U.S.) Tennessee State University (U.S.) United Kingdom Universities Queen Mary University (U.K.) University of Westminster (U.K.) City, University of London (U.K.) University of Greenwich (U.K.) Have a minimum grade point average of 2.75 on a 4.0 scale, or its equivalent Preference will be given to students pursuing a degree in one of the following fields: Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, Machine Learning, Mathematics, Statistics, Life Sciences, Marketing, Finance, Business Economics, Business Management, Cybersecurity, or User Experience. Ancestry employees and their immediate family members (spouses, children, and grandchildren) are ineligible.

records.title: Brave of Heart Scholarship
records.description: The Brave of Heart Scholarship supports the children (age 26 and under), spouses or domestic partners of frontline healthcare workers who lost their lives to COVID-related causes.
records.eligibility: wysiwyg_basic Eligible applicants must be U.S. citizens or legal residents who plan to enroll, full-time or part-time, in undergraduate or graduate study at an accredited two- or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school in the upcoming academic year. Applicants must also have a GPA of 2.0 on a 4.0 scale or its equivalent. Applicants of the Brave of Heart Scholarship must: Be a child, spouse or domestic partner of a frontline healthcare worker who lost their life to a COVID-19-related cause. Child is defined as a biological, step- or legally adopted child who is age 26 and under as of the application deadline date. The child must be living in the frontline healthcare worker’s household or primarily supported by the frontline healthcare worker. If the child is enrolled in a graduate school program, they must be age 26 and under and may be financially dependent or independent to be eligible. The Brave of Heart Scholarships is available for children who first apply and receive an award by age 26. To continue receiving scholarship assistance beyond age 26, children must then continue to apply for the Brave of Heart Scholarship (uninterrupted) and maintain continuous enrollment in their program (uninterrupted), with the exception of summer vacation. Frontline healthcare worker is defined as a person who lived in the United States at the time of death and worked or volunteered in or for a licensed hospital, medical center or clinic, nursing home, medical transport vehicle, triage center, or other licensed medical facility, provider, or setting, or who worked or volunteered as an emergency medical technician, ambulance technician or paramedic. The individual must have had the possibility of exposure to patients with COVID-19 while working or volunteering Plan to enroll full-time or part-time in an undergraduate or graduate program (graduate program must have a patient-facing medical major). See Awards section for definition of full-time and part-time. Plan to attend an accredited vocational-technical school, two- or four-year college or university, or graduate school. Have a minimum grade point average of 2.0 on a 4.0 scale or its equivalent. Non-traditional students are encouraged to apply, and will be considered even if they do not have a recent GPA. Be a United States (U.S.) citizen or legal resident living in and attending an educational institution in the U.S. or a U.S. territory. Study abroad programs may be eligible courses of study if run through an educational institution in the U.S. or a U.S. territory. Ineligible occupations include non-medical frontline workers, such as supermarket employees, delivery workers, ride-share drivers, funeral home staff, and police. Firefighters are also ineligible unless certified EMTs or paramedics. Other occupations may be ineligible and are evaluated at the sole discretion of the sponsor.
